title.zh: 卷三 帝紀第三 世祖武帝
title.raw: 卷三 帝紀第三 世祖武帝 Volume 3 Annals 3: Emperor Wu

sentences.zh: 武皇帝諱炎，字安世，文帝長子也。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor's taboo name was Yan, his style name Anshi; he was the eldest son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored posthumously as Wu bore the personal name Yan and the courtesy name Anshi; he was the firstborn son of Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao).

sentences.zh: 寬惠仁厚，沈深有度量。

translations.literal: He was generous, kind, and humane in his magnanimity, deep and reserved, with breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Broad-minded, humane, and gentle by nature, he was grave and self-contained, with the measured bearing of a true ruler.

sentences.zh: 魏嘉平中，封北平亭侯，歷給事中、奉車都尉、中壘將軍，加散騎常侍，累遷中護軍、假節。

translations.literal: In the Jiaping era of Wei he was enfeoffed as marquis of Beipingting, then served successively as gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, with additional appointment as regular palace attendant of cavalier, and was repeatedly promoted to central protector with plenary authority.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei’s Jiaping years he received the Beipingting marquisate and rose through a string of palace and guard posts—gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary—until he became central protector, bearing the yellow staff of full authority.

sentences.zh: 迎常道鄉公於東武陽，遷中撫軍，進封新昌鄉侯。

translations.literal: He welcomed the duke of Changdaoxiang at Dongwuyang, was transferred to central commander of the army, and advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Xinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongwuyang he received the duke of Changdaoxiang, was named central commander of the army, and was promoted to marquis of Xinxiang.

sentences.zh: 及晉國建，立爲世子，拜撫軍大將軍，開府、副貳相國。

translations.literal: When the state of Jin was founded he was established as heir apparent, appointed great general who pacifies the army with independent command, and served as deputy to the minister of state.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jin polity was erected, he was made heir apparent and great general who pacifies the army, with his own headquarters, assisting the minister of state as second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝以景帝既宣帝之嫡，早世無後，以帝弟攸爲嗣，特加愛異，自謂攝居相位，百年之後，大業宜歸攸。

translations.literal: At first, because prince Jing (Sima Shi), as the legitimate heir of emperor Xuan, had died young without posterity, emperor Wen had taken the emperor's younger brother You as successor and shown him exceptional favor; believing himself only provisionally to hold the chancellorship, he expected that after his death the great enterprise ought to pass to You.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wen had adopted his brother You as heir because prince Jing—Xuan’s rightful line—had left no sons; Wen doted on You and assumed that, as regent for the time being, the throne would one day be You’s.

sentences.zh: 每曰：「此景王之天下也，吾何與焉。

translations.literal: He would often say, "This is prince Jing's realm; what have I to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of saying, “This is really prince Jing’s world, not mine.”

sentences.zh: 」將議立世子，屬意於攸。

translations.literal: When they were about to deliberate on installing the heir apparent, his inclination settled on You.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came to choose an heir, his heart was set on You.

sentences.zh: 何曾等固爭曰：「中撫軍聰明神武，有超世之才。

translations.literal: He Zeng and others firmly argued, saying, "The central commander of the army is astute, martial, and divinely awe-inspiring; he has talents surpassing the age."
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng and his colleagues pressed the point: the central commander was brilliant, formidable, and clearly born for greatness.

sentences.zh: 髮委地，手過膝，此非人臣之相也。

translations.literal: "His hair trails to the ground and his hands pass his knees; these are not the features of a minister."
translations.idiomatic: “His hair reaches the floor and his hands hang below the knees—marks of a sovereign, not a subject.”

sentences.zh: 」由是遂定。

translations.literal: On this account the matter was finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis the choice was fixed.

sentences.zh: 咸熙二年五月，立爲晉王太子。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Xianxi he was established as crown prince of the king of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianxi 2, fifth month, he was named crown prince to the king of Jin.

sentences.zh: 八月辛卯，文帝崩，太子嗣相國、晉王位。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao of the eighth month emperor Wen died; the crown prince succeeded to the offices of minister of state and king of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in the eighth month Wen died, and the crown prince inherited both the minister of state’s portfolio and the kingship of Jin.

sentences.zh: 下令寬刑宥罪，撫眾息役，國內行服三日。

translations.literal: He issued orders to lighten punishments and pardon crimes, console the people and halt corvée labor, and for three days within the state mourning dress was worn.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered clemency, tax relief in spirit, and an end to forced labor, while the court wore mourning for three days.

sentences.zh: 是月，長人見於襄武，長三丈，告縣人王始曰：「今當太平。」

translations.literal: That month a man of extraordinary height appeared at Xiangwu, three zhang tall, and announced to the people of the district, Wang Shi, "Now there shall be great peace."
translations.idiomatic: That month a giant figure, said to stand three zhang high, was seen at Xiangwu and told the locals, among them Wang Shi, that an age of peace was at hand.

sentences.zh: 九月戊午，以魏司徒何曾爲丞相，鎮南將軍王沈爲御史大夫，中護軍賈充爲衛將軍，議郎裴秀爲尚書令、光祿大夫，皆開府。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu of the ninth month he appointed He Zeng, steward of Wei, as chancellor; Wang Chen, general who guards the south, as imperial counselor; Jia Chong, central protector, as guard general; Pei Xiu, gentleman in discussion, as supervisor of the masters of writing and grand officer of brilliant prosperity—all with independent commands.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu in the ninth month he formed his core cabinet: He Zeng as chancellor, Wang Chen as imperial counselor, Jia Chong as guard general, Pei Xiu as supervisor of the masters of writing and grand officer of brilliant prosperity, each with full general’s establishment.

sentences.zh: 十一月，初置四護軍，以統城外諸軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he first established four army protectors to command all the armies outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he created four “army protector” posts to oversee every garrison beyond the capital.

sentences.zh: 乙未，令諸郡中正以六條舉淹滯：一曰忠恪匪躬，二曰孝敬盡禮，三曰友于兄弟，四曰潔身勞謙，五曰信義可復，六曰學以爲己。

translations.literal: On yiwei he ordered the middle (district) heads of commanderies to recommend the long-neglected and obstructed according to six criteria: first, loyalty and conscientiousness sacrificing self; second, filial respect fulfilling ritual; third, harmony among brothers; fourth, purity of person with humble industry; fifth, trustworthiness and righteousness that can be relied upon; sixth, learning for one’s own moral cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei he told commandery “middle” heads to lift up stalled talent under six rubrics—loyal service, filial piety, fraternal harmony, modest integrity, reliable good faith, and learning pursued for its own sake.

sentences.zh: 是時晉德既洽，四海宅心。

translations.literal: At this time the virtue of Jin had already permeated the realm, and all within the four seas made it their home.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jin’s moral authority had spread so widely that the empire looked to it as the natural center.

sentences.zh: 於是天子知曆數有在，乃使太保鄭沖奉策曰：「咨爾晉王：我皇祖有虞氏誕膺靈運，受終于陶唐，亦以命于有夏。

translations.literal: Thereupon the son of heaven knew that the celestial mandate rested with Jin, and sent grand guardian Zheng Chong to present the edict, saying, "I address you, king of Jin: Our august ancestor Youyu received the numinous fortune and accepted the abdication from Tao Tang; likewise he enjoined Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Heaven’s favor had shifted, the Wei emperor dispatched grand guardian Zheng Chong with a deed of abdication: “King of Jin—from Shun’s receipt of Yao’s mandate down to Xia—the line has always been clear.

sentences.zh: 惟三后陟配于天，而咸用光敷聖德。

translations.literal: The three later sovereigns ascended to match heaven, and all alike spread abroad their sagely power.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the three sage-kings rose to partner Heaven and spread his virtue abroad.

sentences.zh: 自茲厥後，天又輯大命于漢。

translations.literal: From that time onward heaven again gathered the great mandate upon Han.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Heaven gathered the mandate once more in Han.

sentences.zh: 火德既衰，乃眷命我高祖。

translations.literal: When the virtue of fire had waned, it then turned its favor to our high ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When Han’s “fire” virtue faded, it looked to our founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 方軌虞夏四代之明顯，我不敢知。

translations.literal: Whether we parallel the luminous models of Yu, Xia, and the two intervening reigns, I dare not claim to know.
translations.idiomatic: Whether we truly match the luminous succession of Yu, Xia, and what lies between—I would not presume to say.

sentences.zh: 惟王乃祖乃父，服膺明哲，輔亮我皇家，勳德光于四海。

translations.literal: Only your ancestors and fathers embraced enlightened wisdom and assisted our royal house; their merit and virtue shone throughout the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your forebears, generation after generation, served our dynasty with enlightened wisdom; their achievements lit the realm.

sentences.zh: 格爾上下神祇，罔不克順，地平天成，萬邦以乂。

translations.literal: You have moved the spirits high and low; none have failed to obey; earth is level and heaven complete, and the myriad regions are well governed.
translations.idiomatic: You have won the assent of gods above and below; the cosmos is ordered and every land is ruled aright.

sentences.zh: 應受上帝之命，協皇極之中。

translations.literal: You ought to receive the charge of the high lord and harmonize the supreme pivot.
translations.idiomatic: You are fit to take up Heaven’s charge and hold the central balance of the realm.

sentences.zh: 肆予一人，祗承天序，以敬授爾位，曆數實在爾躬。

translations.literal: Therefore I, the solitary man, reverently accept the celestial sequence and respectfully transmit to you your position; the reckoning of the mandate is truly in your person.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I, humble as I am, bow to the succession of Heaven and solemnly hand you the throne—the mandate plainly rests with you.

sentences.zh: 允執其中，天祿永終。

translations.literal: Faithfully hold the mean; heaven’s blessing will be endless.
translations.idiomatic: Hold fast to the middle way, and Heaven’s favor will not end.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Oh!

sentences.zh: 王其欽順天命。

translations.literal: May the king respectfully obey heaven’s command.
translations.idiomatic: May you, king, bow to what Heaven commands.

sentences.zh: 率循訓典，底綏四國，用保天休，無替我二皇之弘烈。

translations.literal: Follow the models and canons, bring peace to the four quarters, thereby to preserve heaven’s grace, and do not replace the grand enterprise of our two august predecessors.
translations.idiomatic: Walk in the tracks of the classics, pacify the four quarters, secure Heaven’s favor, and do not dishonor the mighty work of our two sage predecessors.”

sentences.zh: 」帝初以禮讓，魏朝公卿何曾、王沈等固請，乃從之。

translations.literal: At first the emperor demurred on grounds of ritual propriety, but the dukes and ministers of Wei, He Zeng, Wang Chen, and others pressed him firmly, and he then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The new sovereign first declined out of courtesy, yet He Zeng, Wang Chen, and the rest of the Wei court insisted until he yielded.

sentences.zh: 泰始元年冬十二月丙寅，設壇于南郊，百僚在位及匈奴南單于四夷會者數萬人，柴燎告類于上帝曰：「皇帝臣炎敢用玄牡明告于皇皇后帝：魏帝稽協皇運，紹天明命以命炎。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, winter, twelfth month, first year of Taishi, he set up an altar south of the suburbs; the hundred officials stood in place, together with the southern chanyu of the Xiongnu and visitors from the four barbarians numbering in the tens of thousands; he kindled the firewood offering and reported the category of his accession to the high lord, saying, "The emperor, your subject Yan, dares to use a black bull clearly to announce to august heaven and august earth: the Wei emperor has examined and aligned with the royal fortune and, clarifying heaven’s bright mandate, has used it to command Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On Taishi 1, twelfth month, bingyin, he sacrificed south of the city before a host of officials, foreign chiefs, and onlookers by the tens of thousands, declaring to Heaven and Earth that the Wei ruler had recognized the mandate and named him successor.

sentences.zh: 昔者唐堯，熙隆大道，禪位虞舜，舜又以禪禹，邁德垂訓，多歷年載。

translations.literal: Of old Tang Yao illumined the great way, abdicated the throne to Yu Shun, and Shun again abdicated to Yu, handing down virtue and leaving instructions, through many years.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Yao illumined the great Dao, yielded to Shun, and Shun to Yu—virtue handed down through long ages.

sentences.zh: 暨漢德既衰，太祖武皇帝撥亂濟時，扶翼劉氏，又用受命于漢。

translations.literal: When Han’s virtue had declined, our first ancestor, the martial emperor, rescued the age from chaos and aided the house of Liu, and again received the mandate from Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Han faltered, our martial progenitor quelled disorder and upheld the Liu house, then took his mandate from Han in turn.

sentences.zh: 粵在魏室，仍世多故，幾於顛墜，實賴有晉匡拯之德，用獲保厥肆祀，弘濟于艱難，此則晉之有大造于魏也。

translations.literal: As for the house of Wei, generation after generation met many troubles and nearly toppled; truly it relied on Jin’s power of rescue and support to preserve its sacrifices, and broadly to deliver them through hardship—this means that Jin performed a great service for Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei, reign after reign tottered on the brink; only Jin’s rescue allowed the altars to survive—Jin had indeed saved Wei from ruin.

sentences.zh: 誕惟四方，罔不祗順，廓清梁岷，包懷揚越，八紘同軌，祥瑞屢臻，天人協應，無思不服。

translations.literal: Then as for the four quarters, none failed to revere and obey; Liang and Min were cleared, Yang and Yue embraced; the eight cords shared one track, auspicious omens arrived repeatedly, heaven and man responded in concert, and none who thought did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The four quarters submitted; Liang and Min were pacified, Yang and Yue brought within the fold; omens multiplied, heaven and humankind agreed, and none withheld allegiance.

sentences.zh: 肆予憲章三后，用集大命于茲。

translations.literal: Therefore I take as my model the three later sovereigns and hereby gather the great mandate here.
translations.idiomatic: So I model myself on the three sage-kings and gather the great mandate in this place.

sentences.zh: 炎維德不嗣，辭不獲命。

translations.literal: I, Yan, in virtue am not heir to my predecessors, yet in words I cannot reject the command.
translations.idiomatic: I, Yan, lack virtue enough to inherit this, yet I cannot refuse what is spoken.

sentences.zh: 於是群公卿士，百辟庶僚，黎獻陪隸，暨于百蠻君長，僉曰：『皇天鑒下，求人之瘼，既有成命，固非克讓所得距違。

translations.literal: Thereupon the host of dukes and ministers, the hundred nobles and myriad officials, the commoners and retainers, down to the chiefs of the hundred barbarians, all said, ‘August heaven looks down and seeks out the people’s distress; the completed mandate already exists—indeed it is not something that modest refusal may refuse.’
translations.idiomatic: Then every rank of official and every barbarian chief declared that Heaven had fixed its choice and modesty could not set it aside.

sentences.zh: 天序不可以無統，人神不可以曠主。

translations.literal: The sequence of heaven may not lack a ruler; the gods and men may not long lack a lord.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s line cannot go without a sovereign; gods and men cannot long be without a master.”

sentences.zh: 』炎虔奉皇運，寅畏天威，敬簡元辰，升壇受禪，告類上帝，永答眾望。

translations.literal: I, Yan, reverently uphold the royal fortune, stand in awe of heaven’s majesty, respectfully choose the primary day, ascend the altar and receive the abdication, report the category to the high lord, and forever answer the multitude’s expectation.
translations.idiomatic: I, Yan, therefore reverence Heaven’s course, choose an auspicious day, mount the altar, receive the abdication, inform the high lord, and answer the hopes of all.”

sentences.zh: 」禮畢，即洛陽宮幸太極前殿，詔曰：「昔朕皇祖宣王，聖哲欽明，誕應期運，熙帝之載，肇啟洪基。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished he went at once to the palace at Luoyang and visited the hall before Taiji in the front palace, and issued an edict, saying, "Of old my august grandfather, king Xuan, was sage-like, wise, and discerning; he responded to the period’s fortune and illumined the emperor’s burden, thereby opening the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony done, he entered Luoyang’s Taiji front hall and proclaimed: “My royal grandfather Xuan was a sage who met his age and laid our house’s foundation.

sentences.zh: 伯考景王，履道宣猷，緝熙諸夏。

translations.literal: My uncle, prince Jing, walked the way and spread his plans, continuing the brightness among all Xia.
translations.idiomatic: My uncle prince Jing walked in the Way and extended his rule through the central lands.

sentences.zh: 至于皇考文王，叡哲光遠，允協靈祇，應天順時，受茲明命。

translations.literal: As for my august father, king Wen, profoundly wise and far-seeing, he truly harmonized with the numinous powers, responded to heaven and complied with the season, and received this bright mandate.
translations.idiomatic: My father king Wen, far-sighted and wise, moved spirits and seasons alike and received the bright mandate.

sentences.zh: 仁濟于宇宙，功格于上下。

translations.literal: His benevolence reached to the universe; his merit matched heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: His kindness filled the cosmos; his merit spanned heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 肆魏氏弘鑒于古訓，儀刑于唐虞，疇咨群后，爰輯大命于朕身。

translations.literal: Therefore the house of Wei broadly took mirror from ancient instructions and took law from Tang and Yu, consulted the host of later kings, and thereupon gathered the great mandate upon my person.
translations.idiomatic: So Wei, looking to antiquity like Yao and Shun, consulted the lords and laid the mandate on me.

sentences.zh: 予一人畏天之命，用不敢違。

translations.literal: I, the solitary man, stand in awe of heaven’s command and therefore dare not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: I stand in awe of Heaven and dare not refuse.

sentences.zh: 惟朕寡德，負荷洪烈，託于王公之上，以君臨四海，惴惴惟懼，罔知所濟。

translations.literal: Only I am of scant virtue and bear the mighty enterprise; I rely on the kings and dukes above to face the four seas, trembling in fear, not knowing how to cross.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of slender merit yet I must bear this vast charge; resting on my nobles I rule all under heaven, anxious and unsure how to succeed.

sentences.zh: 惟爾股肱爪牙之佐，文武不貳之臣，乃祖乃父，實左右我先王，光隆我大業。

translations.literal: Only you, assistants as arms and legs and claws and fangs, ministers civil and military who do not serve two masters, your ancestors and fathers, truly aided our former kings and made radiant our great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: You who are my ministers—civil and military, loyal as bone and sinew—your fathers aided my forebears and built this great work.

sentences.zh: 思與萬國，共享休祚。

translations.literal: I desire together with the myriad states to share good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to share this blessing with every principality.”

sentences.zh: 」於是大赦，改元。

translations.literal: Thereupon he declared a great amnesty and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and a new era name.

sentences.zh: 賜天下爵，人五級；

translations.literal: He bestowed noble ranks on the empire, five grades per person;
translations.idiomatic: Every household gained five steps in rank.

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨不能自存者穀，人五斛。

translations.literal: To widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless who could not support themselves he gave grain, five hu per person.
translations.idiomatic: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the destitute received five hu of grain each.

sentences.zh: 復天下租賦及關市之稅一年，逋債宿負皆勿收。

translations.literal: He remitted the empire’s land tax, labor surtax, and market tolls for one year, and long-standing debts and overdue obligations were all not collected.
translations.idiomatic: Land taxes, surcharges, and market dues were forgiven for a year, and old debts were written off.

sentences.zh: 除舊嫌，解禁錮，亡官失爵者悉復之。

translations.literal: He removed old grudges, lifted prohibitions and exclusions, and all who had lost office or rank were fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Old feuds were pardoned, political bans lifted, and everyone stripped of office or title was reinstated.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，遣太僕劉原告于太廟。

translations.literal: On dingmao he sent grand coachman Liu Yuan to announce the matter in the grand temple.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he dispatched grand coachman Liu Yuan to report to the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 封魏帝爲陳留王，邑萬戶，居於鄴宮；

translations.literal: He enfeoffed the Wei emperor as king of Chenliu, with ten thousand households, dwelling in the Ye palace;
translations.idiomatic: The last Wei sovereign became king of Chenliu with a fief of ten thousand households, residing at Ye.

sentences.zh: 魏氏諸王皆爲縣侯。

translations.literal: All kings of the house of Wei were made county marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Every other Wei prince was reduced to county marquis.

sentences.zh: 追尊宣王爲宣皇帝，景王爲景皇帝，文王爲文皇帝，宣王妃張氏爲宣穆皇后。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored king Xuan as emperor Xuan, king Jing as emperor Jing, king Wen as emperor Wen, and king Xuan’s consort, lady Zhang, as empress Xuanmu.
translations.idiomatic: He canonized Xuan, Jing, and Wen as emperors and named Zhang, Xuan’s consort, empress Xuanmu.

sentences.zh: 尊太妃王氏曰皇太后，宮曰崇化。

translations.literal: He honored grand consort Wang as empress dowager, her residence titled Chonghua.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang, the grand consort, became empress dowager with her palace named Chonghua.

sentences.zh: 封皇叔祖父孚爲安平王，皇叔父幹爲平原王，亮爲扶風王，伷爲東莞王，駿爲汝陰王，肜爲梁王，倫爲琅邪王，皇弟攸爲齊王，鑒爲樂安王，機爲燕王，[1]皇從伯父望爲義陽王，皇從叔父輔爲渤海王，晃爲下邳王，瑰爲太原王，珪爲高陽王，衡爲常山王，子文爲沛王，[2]泰爲隴西王，權爲彭城王，綏爲范陽王，遂爲濟南王，遜爲譙王，睦爲中山王，陵爲北海王，斌爲陳王，皇從父兄洪爲河間王，皇從父弟楙爲東平王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed his granduncle Sima Fu as king of Anping, his uncles Sima Gan as king of Pingyuan, Liang as king of Fufeng, Zhou as king of Dongguan, Jun as king of Ru'yin, Tong as king of Liang, Lun as king of Langye, his younger brother You as king of Qi, Jian as king of Le'an, Ji as king of Yan, [1] his cousin once removed Wang as king of Yiyang, his uncles Fu as king of Bohai, Huang as king of Xiapi, Gui as king of Taiyuan, Gui as king of Gaoyang, Heng as king of Changshan, Ziwen as king of Pei, [2] Tai as king of Longxi, Quan as king of Pengcheng, Sui as king of Fanyang, Sui as king of Jinan, Xun as king of Qiao, Mu as king of Zhongshan, Ling as king of Beihai, Bin as king of Chen, his cousin Hong as king of Hejian, and his cousin Mao as king of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: A sweep of enfeoffments followed: granduncle Fu as king of Anping, a ring of royal uncles and cousins as kings of Pingyuan, Fufeng, Dongguan, Ru'yin, Liang, Langye, and more, his brother You as king of Qi, and dozens of kinsmen given kingdoms from Bohai to Dongping (footnotes [1][2] preserved in the text).

sentences.zh: 以驃騎將軍石苞爲大司馬，封樂陵公，車騎將軍陳騫爲高平公，衛將軍賈充爲車騎將軍、魯公，尚書令裴秀爲鉅鹿公，侍中荀勖爲濟北公，太保鄭沖爲太傅、壽光公，太尉王祥爲太保、睢陵公，丞相何曾爲太尉、朗陵公，御史大夫王沈爲驃騎將軍、博陵公，司空荀顗爲臨淮公，鎮北大將軍衛瓘爲菑陽公。

translations.literal: He appointed Shi Bao, general of swift cavalry, as grand marshal with enfeoffment as duke of Leling; Chen Qian, general of chariots and cavalry, as duke of Gaoping; Jia Chong, guard general, as general of chariots and cavalry and duke of Lu; Pei Xiu, supervisor of the masters of writing, as duke of Julu; Xun Xu, palace attendant, as duke of Jibei; Zheng Chong, grand guardian, as grand tutor and duke of Shouguang; Wang Xiang, grand commandant, as grand protector and duke of Suiling; He Zeng, chancellor, as grand commandant and duke of Langling; Wang Chen, imperial counselor, as general of swift cavalry and duke of Boling; Xun Yi, minister of works, as duke of Linhuai; Wei Guan, great general who guards the north, as duke of Ziyang.
translations.idiomatic: The chief generals and ministers received ducal fiefs—Shi Bao grand marshal of Leling, Chen Qian of Gaoping, Jia Chong elevated to chariots-and-cavalry general and duke of Lu, Pei Xiu duke of Julu, and so through the senior statesmen.

sentences.zh: 其餘增封進爵各有差，文武普增位二等。

translations.literal: The rest received increased fiefs and advanced noble ranks each according to difference; civil and military officials were universally advanced two grades in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Others were promoted in title by degrees, and the whole bureaucracy gained two steps in rank.

sentences.zh: 改景初曆爲太始曆，臘以酉，社以丑。

translations.literal: He changed the Jingchu calendar to the Taishi calendar, with year-end sacrifice in the you hour and earth god in the chou hour.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar was renamed from Jingchu to Taishi; the year-end rite was fixed in you and the soil altar in chou.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，下詔大弘儉約，出御府珠玉玩好之物，頒賜王公以下各有差。

translations.literal: On wuchen he issued an edict greatly promoting frugality, bringing out pearls, jade, and curios from the imperial treasury and distributing them to the kings and dukes downward, each according to a scale.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he called for austerity, handing out palace jewels and playthings to princes and nobles by graded gift.

sentences.zh: 置中軍將軍，以統宿衛七軍。

translations.literal: He established the general of the central army to command the seven palace-guard armies.
translations.idiomatic: He created the post of general of the central army over seven inner garrisons.

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔陳留王載天子旌旗，備五時副車，行魏正朔，郊祀天地，禮樂制度皆如魏舊，上書不稱臣。

translations.literal: On jisi he decreed that the king of Chenliu might use the Son of Heaven’s banners, maintain the five seasonal spare chariots, follow Wei’s calendar, sacrifice to heaven and earth, and keep music and ritual as under Wei, while memorials to him need not style the writer a subject.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the Chenliu king was allowed imperial pennons, five seasonal chariots, Wei’s calendar, full suburban rites, and Wei-style court music, with the privilege that petitioners omit the phrase “your subject.”

sentences.zh: 賜山陽公劉康、安樂公劉禪子弟一人爲駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He granted one descendant each of the mountain-yang duke Liu Kang and the duke of peace and ease Liu Shan the post of commandant of the consorts’ escort.
translations.idiomatic: One son or grandson each of Liu Kang, the mountain-yang duke, and Liu Shan, the duke of peace and ease, was named commandant of the consorts’ escort.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以安平王孚爲太宰、假黃鉞、大都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: On yihai he appointed king Fu of Anping as grand preceptor, with the yellow axe as credential and grand commander of all military affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Sima Fu, king of Anping, became grand preceptor, bearing the yellow axe as grand commander of all armies.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔王淩謀廢齊王，而王竟不足以守位。

translations.literal: The edict said, "Of old Wang Ling plotted to depose the prince of Qi, yet the king in the end proved unable to keep his position.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: “Wang Ling once tried to unseat the prince of Qi, yet Qi still could not hold the throne.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾雖矜功失節，然束手受罪。

translations.literal: Deng Ai, though proud of his merit and faulty in restraint, yet bound his hands and accepted punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai, for all his arrogance, surrendered himself for judgment.

sentences.zh: 今大赦其家，還使立後。

translations.literal: Now I declare a great amnesty for his family and send orders that an heir be established for him.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore pardon his household and allow a successor to be named.

sentences.zh: 興滅繼絕，約法省刑。

translations.literal: Raise what was destroyed and continue what was cut off; simplify the laws and lighten punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Restore ruined lines, lighten the code, and ease penalties.

sentences.zh: 除魏氏宗室禁錮。

translations.literal: He removed prohibitions and exclusions on the Wei imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei imperial clan was freed from house arrest and blacklist.

sentences.zh: 諸將吏遭三年喪者，遣寧終喪。

translations.literal: For officers and clerks observing the three-year mourning for parents, he allowed them to remain until mourning was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Any official in the three-year mourning for a parent could stay home until the rites were done.

sentences.zh: 百姓復其傜役。

translations.literal: The common people had their labor services remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners were excused from corvée.

sentences.zh: 罷部曲將長吏以下質任。

translations.literal: He abolished the hostage requirement for commandants and local heads below chief of private troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hostages once demanded of prefects and lower officers under hereditary generals were ended.

sentences.zh: 省郡國御調，禁樂府靡麗百戲之伎及雕文游畋之具。

translations.literal: He cut the court’s special levies on commanderies and principalities, forbade the music bureau’s extravagant acrobatics, and ornamented hunting gear.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery “palace” surcharges were dropped, and the music office was barred from lavish shows and carved hunting toys.

sentences.zh: 開直言之路，置諫官以掌之。」

translations.literal: He opened a road for blunt speech and appointed remonstrance officials to manage it."
translations.idiomatic: He invited frank criticism and set up remonstrators to channel it.”

sentences.zh: 是月，鳳皇六、青龍三、白龍二、麒麟各一見于郡國。

translations.literal: That month phoenixes appeared six times, azure dragons three times, white dragons twice, and unicorns once in the commanderies and principalities.
translations.idiomatic: That month the registers recorded six phoenix sightings, three azure dragons, two white dragons, and a unicorn across the realm.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月丙戌，遣兼侍中侯史光等持節四方，循省風俗，除禳祝之不在祀典者。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, on bingxu he sent concurrent palace attendant Hou Shiguang and others, bearing staffs of authority, to the four directions to tour and inspect customs, and to remove prayers and blessings not listed in the canonical sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 2, spring, first month, bingxu: Hou Shiguang and colleagues toured the empire with imperial staffs, purging illicit shrines not in the ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，有司請建七廟，帝重其役，不許。

translations.literal: On dinghai the offices requested to build seven ancestral temples; the emperor, weighing the labor, did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry asked for seven-temple grandeur; the emperor refused, mindful of the burden.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，罷雞鳴歌。

translations.literal: On gengyin he abolished the “cock-crow” song.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he ended the dawn “cock-crow” anthem at court.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，尊景皇帝夫人羊氏曰景皇后，宮曰弘訓。

translations.literal: On xinchou he honored prince Jing’s consort, lady Yang, as empress Jing, her residence titled Hongxun.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou lady Yang, prince Jing’s widow, became empress Jing with palace name Hongxun.

sentences.zh: 丙午，立皇后楊氏。

translations.literal: On bingwu he established lady Yang as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu he took lady Yang as empress.

sentences.zh: 二月，除漢宗室禁錮。

translations.literal: In the second month he removed prohibitions and exclusions on Han imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Second month: surviving Liu-clan nobles were freed from legal disability.

sentences.zh: 己未，常山王衡薨。

translations.literal: On jiwei king Heng of Changshan died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Sima Heng, king of Changshan, died.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「五等之封，皆錄舊勳。

translations.literal: The edict said, "The enfeoffments of the five ranks all record old merit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict explained that the five-grade nobility rewarded past service.

sentences.zh: 本爲縣侯者傳封次子爲亭侯，鄉侯爲關內侯，[3]亭侯爲關中侯，皆食本戶十分之一。

translations.literal: Those who were originally county marquises transmit enfeoffment to a second son as ting marquis, xiang marquises as marquises within the passes, [3] ting marquises as marquises within Guan, each eating one tenth of the original household.
translations.idiomatic: County marquises could pass a ting marquisate to a younger son; xiang marquises became “inside the passes” marquises [3]; ting marquises became “within Guan” marquises—each at one-tenth of the original income.

sentences.zh: 」丁丑，[4]郊祀宣皇帝以配天，宗祀文皇帝於明堂以配上帝。

translations.literal: On dingchou [4] he sacrificed to heaven at the suburbs with emperor Xuan as correlate, and in the bright hall sacrificed to the high lord with emperor Wen as correlate.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou [4] he paired Xuan with Heaven at the southern suburb and Wen with the high lord in the bright hall.

sentences.zh: 庚午，詔曰：「古者百官，官箴王闕。

translations.literal: On gengwu the edict said, "In antiquity the hundred offices each had maxims for the king’s faults.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he noted that ancient departments each warned the ruler of his errors.

sentences.zh: 然保氏特以諫諍爲職，今之侍中、常侍實處此位。

translations.literal: Yet the guardian alone took remonstrance as his duty; today’s palace attendants and regular attendants truly occupy this role.
translations.idiomatic: The guardian’s special duty was frank advice—now filled by palace and regular attendants.

sentences.zh: 擇其能正色弼違匡救不逮者，以兼此選。」

translations.literal: Choose among them those who can correct color and remedy errors and rescue what is lacking, and let them also hold this selection."
translations.idiomatic: Pick men who will speak truth to power and set them to that very task.”

sentences.zh: 三月戊戌，吳人來弔祭，有司奏爲答詔。

translations.literal: On wuxu of the third month Wu envoys came to offer condolences and sacrifices; the offices memorialized to prepare a reply edict.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, wuxu: Wu’s envoys arrived for the funeral rites, and the clerks drafted a formal answer.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「昔漢文、光武懷撫尉他、公孫述，皆未正君臣之儀，所以羈縻未賓也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Of old Han Wen and Guangwu cherished and soothed Zhao Tuo and Gongsun Shu, and never regularized the rites of ruler and subject, thereby to bind those not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: “Han Wen and Guangwu treated Zhao Tuo and Gongsun Shu generously without forcing full vassal etiquette—that was how they kept half-independent lords in play.

sentences.zh: 皓遣使之始，未知國慶，但以書答之。」

translations.literal: When Hao first sent envoys he did not yet know of our state mourning; I answered only with a letter."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao’s first embassy arrived before he knew we were in mourning; a simple letter sufficed.”

sentences.zh: 夏五月戊辰，詔曰：「陳留王操尚謙沖，每事輒表，非所以優崇之也。

translations.literal: In summer, fifth month, on wuchen the edict said, "The king of Chenliu, Cao Shang, is still modest; on every matter he submits a memorial—this is not the way to show him special honor.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fifth month, wuchen: “The Chenliu king, Cao Shang, still files humble memorials on trifles—that is no way to honor him.

sentences.zh: 主者喻意，非大事皆使王官表上之。

translations.literal: Let the presiding officials make known my intent: except for great matters, have his own officials submit memorials on his behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Tell his staff: hereafter routine business should go up through his own officers, not his personal brush, unless it is weighty.”

sentences.zh: 」壬子，[5]驃騎將軍博陵公王沈卒。

translations.literal: On the day renzi [5], Wang Shen, general of swift cavalry and duke of Boling, died.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi [5] Wang Shen—swift-cavalry general and duke of Boling—passed away.

sentences.zh: 六月壬申，濟南王遂薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day renshen, king Sui of Jinan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renshen, Sima Sui, king of Jinan, died.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛巳，營太廟，致荊山之木，采華山之石；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day xinsi, they built the grand ancestral temple, bringing in timber from Mount Jing and quarrying stone from Mount Hua.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, seventh month, xinsi, work began on the great temple, with logs floated from the Jing range and ashlar cut from Mount Hua.

sentences.zh: 鑄銅柱十二，塗以黃金，鏤以百物，綴以明珠。

translations.literal: They cast twelve bronze pillars, gilded them with gold, carved them with images of the myriad things, and studded them with lustrous pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve bronze columns were cast, sheathed in gold, chased with the hundred emblems, and set with brilliant pearls.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，譙王遜薨。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, king Xun of Qiao died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the king of Qiao, Sima Xun, died.

sentences.zh: 丙午晦，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On the last day of the month, bingwu, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: At month’s end, bingwu, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 八月丙辰，省右將軍官。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day bingchen, the post of general of the right was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, bingchen: the office of general of the right was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 初，帝雖從漢魏之制，既葬除服，而深衣素冠，降席撤膳，哀敬如喪者。

translations.literal: At first, although the emperor followed Han and Wei regulations and doffed mourning after the burial, he wore plain deep garments and an undyed cap, lowered his mat, and withdrew rich foods from his table, grieving with the reverence of one still in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had formally left mourning under Han–Wei precedent, he continued to dress plainly, eat simply, and keep the demeanor of a bereaved son.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，有司奏改服進膳，不許，遂禮終而後復吉。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen the offices memorialized that he change to normal dress and resume a full diet; he did not grant it, and only when the mourning rites were complete did he return to auspicious observance.
translations.idiomatic: Officials begged him on wuchen to set aside austerity; he refused until the last ritual day had passed.

sentences.zh: 及太后之喪，亦如之。

translations.literal: When it came to the mourning for the empress dowager, he acted in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: At the empress dowager’s death he observed the same severe restraint.

sentences.zh: 九月乙未，散騎常侍皇甫陶、傅玄領諫官，上書諫諍，有司奏請寢之。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei of the ninth month, the regular attendants of cavalier Huangfu Tao and Fu Xuan headed the remonstrance officials and submitted memorials of criticism; the offices memorialized to shelve them.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in the ninth month Huangfu Tao and Fu Xun, as remonstrators, sent up blunt advice; the clerks moved to bury their petitions.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「凡關言人主，人臣所至難，而苦不能聽納，自古忠臣直士之所慷慨也。

translations.literal: An edict said: “In all that touches remonstrating with the sovereign, a subject’s task is hardest of all, yet the bitter inability to listen and accept has stirred loyal ministers and upright men from antiquity onward.”
translations.idiomatic: He replied: “Speaking truth to a ruler is the hardest duty a minister bears, and rulers who will not hear it have always broken the hearts of the faithful.”

sentences.zh: 每陳事出付主者，多從深刻，乃云恩貸當由主上，是何言乎？

translations.literal: Whenever memorials were handed to handlers, they mostly pursued severity; then they would say gracious pardons must come from the throne—what manner of talk is that?
translations.idiomatic: Too often papers were passed to clerks who pressed the harshest reading and then claimed mercy was solely the emperor’s affair.

sentences.zh: 其詳評議。」

translations.literal: Let them deliberate this in full detail.”
translations.idiomatic: Have every office review this carefully and report.”

sentences.zh: 戊戌，有司奏：「大晉繼三皇之蹤，蹈舜禹之跡，應天順時，受禪有魏，宜一用前代正朔服色，皆如虞遵唐故事。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu the offices memorialized: “Great Jin treads in the footsteps of the Three Sovereigns, follows the tracks of Shun and Yu, complies with heaven and the times, and received the abdication from Wei; it should uniformly adopt the calendar and regalia of former dynasties, entirely as when Yu followed Tang’s precedent.”
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu ministers argued that Jin, heir to the sage-kings and recipient of Wei’s abdication, ought to standardize calendar and court dress on ancient models, as Yu had once followed Tang.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙午朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day bingwu, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, new moon on bingwu: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丁未，詔曰：「昔舜葬蒼梧，農不易畝；

translations.literal: On the day dingwei an edict said: “Of old, when Shun was buried at Cangwu, farmers did not change their fields.”
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he cited antiquity: “When Shun lay at Cangwu, no ploughman had to move his furrow.”

sentences.zh: 禹葬成紀，市不改肆。

translations.literal: When Yu was buried at Chengji, markets did not change their stalls.”
translations.idiomatic: When Yu rested at Chengji, shopkeepers kept the same stalls.”

sentences.zh: 上惟祖考清簡之旨，所徙陵十里內居人，動爲煩擾，一切停之。」

translations.literal: Reflecting on the clear and simple intent of my ancestors, the removal of commoners dwelling within ten li of the mausoleum sites would stir needless trouble; all such relocations are halted.”
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of my forebears’ love of simplicity, I stop every plan to uproot households within ten li of the imperial tombs.”

sentences.zh: 十一月己卯，倭人來獻方物。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jimao, people of Wa came to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, jimao: envoys from Wa arrived with tribute.

sentences.zh: 并圜丘、方丘於南、北郊，二至之祀合於二郊。

translations.literal: The Round Mound and Square Mound were combined at the southern and northern suburban altars; the two solstice sacrifices were united with those two suburban rites.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban ritual was streamlined: the round and square altars were paired with south and north suburb worship, and the solstice services were folded into those sites.

sentences.zh: 罷山陽公國督軍，除其禁制。

translations.literal: The supervisory army of the mountain-yang duke’s state was abolished and its restrictive controls removed.
translations.idiomatic: The military overseer attached to the mountain-yang ducal fief was dismissed and its special prohibitions lifted.

sentences.zh: 己丑，追尊景帝夫人夏侯氏爲景懷皇后。

translations.literal: On the day jichou prince Jing’s consort, the lady of the Xiahou clan, was posthumously honored as empress Jinghuai.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Xiahou, prince Jing’s widow, was canonized as empress Jinghuai.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，遷祖禰神主于太廟。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao the spirit tablets of the distant and immediate ancestors were moved into the grand temple.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the ancestral tablets were carried into the great temple.

sentences.zh: 十二月，罷農官爲郡縣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the agricultural intendancies were abolished and reorganized as commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: That December the old “agriculture” jurisdictions were converted into ordinary counties.

sentences.zh: 是歲，鳳皇六、青龍十、黃龍九、麒麟各一見于郡國。

translations.literal: That year phoenixes appeared six times, azure dragons ten times, yellow dragons nine times, and a unicorn once in the commanderies and principalities.
translations.idiomatic: The year’s omens included six phoenixes, ten azure dragons, nine yellow dragons, and a unicorn reported across the realm.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月癸丑，白龍二見于弘農、澠池。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, first month, on the day guichou, two white dragons were seen at Hongnong and Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 3, spring, guichou: twin white dragons were sighted at Hongnong and Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，[6]立皇子衷爲皇太子。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao [6] the imperial son Zhong was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao [6] Sima Zhong was named heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕以不德，託于四海之上，兢兢祗畏，懼無以康濟宇內，思與天下式明王度，正本清源，於置胤樹嫡，非所先務。

translations.literal: An edict said: “I, lacking in virtue, rely on the realm above me; fearful and reverent, I worry that I cannot bring peace within the four seas, and I wish together with all under heaven to clarify the kingly norms, rectify the root and cleanse the source; as for establishing heirs and fixing the legitimate line, that is not the foremost task at present.”
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed: “I am an unworthy man set over the empire; anxious only to set right the foundations of rule, I do not yet treat the naming of an heir as my first duty.”

sentences.zh: 又近世每建太子，寬宥施惠之事，間不獲已，順從王公卿士之議耳。

translations.literal: Moreover in recent times, whenever a crown prince was installed, the granting of broad pardons and largesse was only an occasional necessity, done to comply with the opinions of kings, dukes, and ministers.”
translations.idiomatic: Lately each new heir brought wholesale amnesties—measures taken only when ministers pressed for them, not because they were inherently right.”

sentences.zh: 方今世運垂平，將陳之以德義，示之以好惡，使百姓蠲多幸之慮，篤終始之行，曲惠小仁，故無取焉。

translations.literal: Now the age’s fortune verges on peace; I shall set forth virtue and duty, show good and evil plainly, so that the people may cast off vain hopes of luck and devote themselves to conduct from first to last; petty favors dressed as kindness are therefore not to be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: As peace nears, I would teach the realm through moral example rather than scatter small mercies that teach the crowd to gamble on fortune.

sentences.zh: 咸使知聞。」

translations.literal: Let all be informed of this.”
translations.idiomatic: Let everyone hear and understand this.”

sentences.zh: 三月戊寅，初令二千石得終三年喪。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day wuyin, it was first ordered that officials at two thousand piculs might observe the full three-year mourning for parents.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, wuyin: for the first time, governors at the two-thousand-picul grade were allowed the full three-year funeral for a parent.

sentences.zh: 丁未，[7]晝昏。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei [7] it was dark at midday.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei [7] daylight failed at noon.

sentences.zh: 罷武衛將軍官。

translations.literal: The post of general who guards the martial guard was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The “martial guard” generalship was eliminated.

sentences.zh: 以李憙爲太子太傅。

translations.literal: Li Xi was appointed grand tutor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi became tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 太山石崩。

translations.literal: Mount Tai’s stone cliffs collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: A cliff face on Mount Tai fell in a landslide.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊午，張掖太守焦勝上言，氐池縣大柳谷口有玄石一所，白畫成文，實大晉之休祥，圖之以獻。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day wuwu, Zhangye prefect Jiao Sheng reported that at the mouth of Great Willow Valley in Dichi county there was a black stone on which characters formed in daylight, truly an auspicious sign for great Jin; he had it drawn and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, wuwu: Jiao Sheng of Zhangye sent up word that a black boulder in Dichi’s Great Willow Gorge had sprouted white-inscribed text—a Jin omen—and enclosed a rubbing.

sentences.zh: 詔以制幣告于太廟，藏之天府。

translations.literal: An edict ordered silks and jade disks to be used in announcement at the grand temple, and the object stored in the celestial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged the omen with ritual silks at the great temple and locked the stone away in the imperial archive.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，罷都護將軍，以其五署還光祿勳。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, the general who protects all armies was abolished, and its five bureaus were returned to the superintendent of the palace gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, eighth month: the “protect all armies” post was cut, its five offices folded back under the superintendent of palace gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 九月甲申，詔曰：「古者以德詔爵，以庸制祿，雖下士猶食上農，外足以奉公忘私，內足以養親施惠。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen of the ninth month an edict said: “In antiquity ranks were proclaimed by virtue, stipends regulated by service; even a low knight still ate like a top farmer, outwardly enough to serve the state and forget private interest, inwardly enough to nourish kin and spread kindness.”
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, jiashen: a long edict recalled how ancient stipends matched real labor so that even minor officers could feed their families and serve without corruption.

sentences.zh: 今在位者祿不代耕，非所以崇化之本也。

translations.literal: Now those in office receive stipends that do not equal the yield of ploughing; this is not the root of promoting transformation.”
translations.idiomatic: Today’s salaries no longer match a farmer’s harvest—that is a poor way to teach honest government.”

sentences.zh: 其議增吏俸。

translations.literal: Let them deliberate increasing clerks’ salaries.”
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a discussion of higher pay for officials.”

sentences.zh: 」賜王公以下帛各有差。

translations.literal: Silks were bestowed on the kings and dukes downward, each according to a scale.”
translations.idiomatic: Silk gifts went out to every rank from princes downward, graded by station.

sentences.zh: 以太尉何曾爲太保，義陽王望爲太尉，司空荀顗爲司徒。

translations.literal: Grand commandant He Zeng was made grand protector; king Wang of Yiyang was made grand commandant; minister of works Xun Yi was made steward of the masters of the people.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng rose to grand protector, Sima Wang of Yiyang to grand commandant, and Xun Yi to steward of the masters of the people.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，聽士卒遭父母喪者，非在疆埸，皆得奔赴。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, soldiers whose parents had died were permitted to hurry home for mourning unless they were on the battlefront.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month: troops mourning parents could leave camp for the funeral unless they stood on an active frontier.

sentences.zh: 十二月，徙宗聖侯孔震爲奉聖亭侯。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the marquis who continues the sage, Kong Zhen, was transferred to be marquis of the village that honors the sage.
translations.idiomatic: December: Kong Zhen, “continuer of the sage,” was moved to the smaller fief of “village that honors the sage.”

sentences.zh: 山陽公劉康來朝。

translations.literal: The mountain-yang duke Liu Kang came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kang, the mountain-yang duke, paid a formal visit.

sentences.zh: 禁星氣讖緯之學。

translations.literal: The study of stellar omens, prognostication, and weft-text apocrypha was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Astrology, prophecy, and apocryphal “weft” learning were banned.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月辛未，以尚書令裴秀爲司空。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the day xinwei, Pei Xiu, supervisor of the masters of writing, was appointed minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, spring, xinwei: Pei Xiu left the secretariat to become minister of works.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，律令成，封爵賜帛各有差。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu the code and ordinances were completed; enfeoffments and silk gifts were distributed each according to difference.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the new code was finished; titles and silk were handed out by grade.

sentences.zh: 有星孛于軫。

translations.literal: A broom star appeared in the asterism Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: A comet blazed across the Zhen mansion in the sky.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，帝耕於藉田。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai the emperor ploughed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the Son of Heaven broke the soil of the ritual field.

sentences.zh: 戊子，詔曰：「古設象刑而眾不犯，今雖參夷而姦不絕，何德刑相去之遠哉！

translations.literal: On the day wuzi an edict said: “In antiquity symbolic punishments were set up yet the multitude did not offend; now though we extend punishment to three kinships wickedness does not cease—how far apart are virtue and punishment!”
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi he mused: “When Yao and Shun relied on symbolic law, crime was rare; today we slaughter whole clans yet treason persists—what has become of moral government?”

sentences.zh: 先帝深愍黎元，哀矜庶獄，乃命群后，考正典刑。

translations.literal: The former emperor deeply pitied the black-haired people and showed compassion in the myriad cases of justice; he therefore ordered the host of later kings to examine and correct the canonical punishments.”
translations.idiomatic: My predecessor pitied the commoners and bade his ministers revise the penal code with mercy.”

sentences.zh: 朕守遺業，永惟保乂皇基，思與萬國以無爲爲政。

translations.literal: I guard the inherited enterprise and ever think to protect and stabilize the royal foundation; I desire together with the myriad regions to govern by non-action.”
translations.idiomatic: I hold his legacy and mean to secure the throne through quiet, sparing rule.”

sentences.zh: 方今陽春養物，東作始興，朕親率王公卿士耕藉田千畝。

translations.literal: Now, in the yang spring that nurtures things, eastern works are just beginning; I have personally led kings, dukes, and ministers to plough one thousand mu of the sacred field.”
translations.idiomatic: As spring work opens in the east, I have led the nobility through the thousand-mu ploughing rite.”

sentences.zh: 又律令既就，班之天下，將以簡法務本，惠育海內。

translations.literal: Moreover, now that the code and ordinances are ready, they will be promulgated to the empire in order to simplify the laws and stress fundamentals, thereby kindly nurturing all within the seas.”
translations.idiomatic: The finished statutes will go to every commandery to streamline justice and nurture the people.”

sentences.zh: 宜寬有罪，使得自新，其大赦天下。

translations.literal: It is fitting to widen mercy to the guilty so they may renew themselves; therefore a great amnesty is declared for the realm.”
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty will let minor offenders begin again.”

sentences.zh: 長吏、郡丞、長史各賜馬一匹。」

translations.literal: Each chief, assistant, and senior clerk is granted one horse.”
translations.idiomatic: Every prefect, aide, and senior clerk receives a horse from the stable.”

sentences.zh: 二月庚子，增置山陽公國相、郎中令、陵令、雜工宰人、鼓吹車馬各有差。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi of the second month posts were added to the mountain-yang duke’s state—a minister, a gentleman director, a tomb intendant, miscellaneous artisans, cooks, and musical ensembles and carriages, each according to scale.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, gengzi: the Chenliu ex-emperor’s apanage gained a full household staff—chancellor, household director, tomb wardens, artisans, cooks, and a band with carriages.

sentences.zh: 罷中軍將軍，置北軍中候官。

translations.literal: The general of the central army was abolished and the post of inspector of the northern armies was established.
translations.idiomatic: The central-army command was deleted in favor of a northern-army inspector.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以東海劉儉有至行，拜爲郎。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin Liu Jian of Donghai, for supreme conduct, was appointed gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Liu Jian of Donghai, famed for virtue, was named a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 以中軍將軍羊祜爲尚書左僕射，東莞王伷爲尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: General of the central army Yang Hu was appointed senior vice-director of the masters of the left; king Zhou of Dongguan was appointed senior vice-director of the right.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu became left vice-president of the secretariat; Sima Zhou of Dongguan became right vice-president.

sentences.zh: 三月戊子，皇太后王氏崩。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi of the third month Empress Dowager Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, wuzi: Empress Dowager Wang passed away.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊戌，太保、睢陵公王祥薨。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu of summer, fourth month, Wang Xiang, grand protector and duke of Suiling, died.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, wuxu: Wang Xiang, grand protector of Suiling, died.

sentences.zh: 己亥，祔葬文明皇后王氏於崇陽陵。

translations.literal: On the day jihai Empress Wenming, lady Wang, was given joint burial at Chongyang mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Empress Wenming was laid beside her husband at Chongyang.

sentences.zh: 罷振威、揚威護軍官，置左右積弩將軍。

translations.literal: The posts of protector generals who display might and raise might were abolished, and generals of the left and right accumulated crossbows were established.
translations.idiomatic: The “display might” and “raise might” protector posts were cut; left and right “accumulated crossbow” generals took their place.

sentences.zh: 六月丙申朔，[8]詔曰：「郡國守相，三載一巡行屬縣，必以春，此古者所以述職宣風展義也。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, bingshen [8], an edict said: “Commandery and principality governors and chiefs shall once every three years tour their subordinate counties, necessarily in spring—this is how antiquity required them to report duty, spread customs, and display righteousness.”
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, new moon, bingshen [8]: governors must every third spring tour their counties, as the classics demanded.

sentences.zh: 見長吏，觀風俗，協禮律，考度量，存問耆老，親見百年。

translations.literal: They shall meet county chiefs, observe local customs, harmonize ritual with law, examine weights and measures, inquire after the aged, and personally visit centenarians.
translations.idiomatic: They are to interview magistrates, watch folkways, align statute with rite, check weights and measures, and greet the very old.

sentences.zh: 錄囚徒，理冤枉，詳察政刑得失，知百姓所患苦。

translations.literal: They shall record prisoners, rectify wrongful judgments, and carefully review whether administration and punishments gain or lose, and know what troubles the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: They must review dockets, reverse injustice, weigh the quality of justice, and learn what pains the people.

sentences.zh: 無有遠近，便若朕親臨之。

translations.literal: Whether near or far, it shall be as if I myself were present.”
translations.idiomatic: Distance must not blunt inspection; each tour should feel like an imperial visit.”

sentences.zh: 敦喻五教，勸務農功，勉勵學者，思勤正典，無爲百家庸末，致遠必泥。

translations.literal: They shall earnestly expound the five teachings, urge agricultural work, encourage students to labor at the correct classics, and not become vulgar pedants of the hundred schools who stick in the mud when seeking what is distant.”
translations.idiomatic: They should preach the five relationships, push farming, urge scholars toward the orthodox canon, and shun the hundred schools’ pedantry.

sentences.zh: 士庶有好學篤道，孝弟忠信，清白異行者，舉而進之；

translations.literal: For gentry and commoners who love learning, cleave to the way, are filial, fraternal, loyal, and faithful, and show unsullied conduct out of the ordinary, recommend and advance them.
translations.idiomatic: Promote any commoner or gentleman who studies deeply, keeps filial piety and good faith, and lives with conspicuous integrity.

sentences.zh: 有不孝敬於父母，不長悌於族黨，悖禮棄常，不率法令者，糾而罪之。

translations.literal: Those who fail to show filial respect to parents or senior kindness within the lineage, who violate ritual and abandon constant norms, or who do not obey statutes and orders, investigate and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Punish unfilial kin, clan troublemakers, and lawbreakers.

sentences.zh: 田疇闢，生業修，禮教設，禁令行，則長吏之能也。

translations.literal: When fields are opened, livelihoods improved, ritual instruction established, and prohibitions enforced—that is the ability of a chief.”
translations.idiomatic: Good magistrates open land, enrich households, teach ritual, and enforce the code.

sentences.zh: 人窮匱，農事荒，姦盜起，刑獄煩，下陵上替，禮義不興，斯長吏之否也。

translations.literal: When people are destitute, farming neglected, banditry rises, litigation piles up, inferiors bully superiors, and ritual and rightness do not flourish—that is the failure of a chief.”
translations.idiomatic: Bad ones leave fields idle, invite theft, clog the courts, and let propriety collapse.

sentences.zh: 若長吏在官公廉，慮不及私，正色直節，不飾名譽者，及身行貪穢，諂黷求容，公節不立，而私門日富者，並謹察之。

translations.literal: If a chief in office is fair and incorrupt, his thoughts do not turn to private gain, his bearing is straight and his integrity unbending, and he does not polish reputation; or if personally he walks the path of greed and filth, flatters and bribes to win favor, public integrity is not set up while private gates grow daily richer—both sorts shall be carefully examined.”
translations.idiomatic: Reward magistrates who stay honest and plain; expose those who grow rich through favor-seeking.

sentences.zh: 揚清激濁，舉善彈違，此朕所以垂拱總綱，責成於良二千石也。

translations.literal: To raise the clear and stir the turbid, to recommend the good and impeach the deviant—this is why I sit with folded arms holding the net’s cords and entrust completion to worthy governors at two thousand piculs.”
translations.idiomatic: That is how I mean to clarify administration from the capital while counting on strong two-thousand-picul men in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 於戲戒哉！」

translations.literal: Oh! Be vigilant!”
translations.idiomatic: Take this order to heart.”

sentences.zh: 秋七月，太山石崩，眾星西流。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Mount Tai’s stone collapsed and hosts of stars streamed westward.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: another cliff fell on Mount Tai while meteors streaked west across the sky.

sentences.zh: 戊午，[9]遣使者侯史光循行天下。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu [9] envoys led by Hou Shiguang were sent to tour the empire.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu [9] Hou Shiguang and other inspectors fanned out across the realm.

sentences.zh: 己卯，謁崇陽陵。

translations.literal: On the day jimao he visited Chongyang mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the emperor paid his respects at Chongyang tomb.

sentences.zh: 九月，青、徐、兗、豫四州大水，伊洛溢，合於河，開倉以振之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the four provinces Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu suffered great floods; the Yi and Luo overflowed and merged with the Yellow River; granaries were opened for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: catastrophic floods in Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu sent the Yi and Luo into the Yellow River; imperial granaries fed the homeless.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「雖詔有所欲，及奏得可而於事不便者，皆不可隱情。」

translations.literal: An edict said: “Although an edict may express what is desired, and although a memorial may be approved, if the matter is inconvenient in practice, none may hide the true situation.”
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that no minister might sit on inconvenient truths even after an edict had passed.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，吳將施績入江夏，萬郁寇襄陽。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Wu general Shi Ji entered Jiangxia, and Wan Yu raided Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month: Wu’s Shi Ji pushed into Jiangxia while Wan Yu struck Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: [10]遣太尉義陽王望屯龍陂。

translations.literal: [10] Grand commandant Sima Wang of Yiyang was sent to encamp at Longpi.
translations.idiomatic: [10] Grand commandant Sima Wang of Yiyang marched to Longpi.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史胡烈擊敗郁。

translations.literal: Jing province inspector Hu Lie defeated Wan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lie, inspector of Jing, routed Wan Yu.

sentences.zh: 吳將顧容寇鬱林，太守毛炅大破之，斬其交州刺史劉俊、將軍修則。

translations.literal: Wu general Gu Rong raided Yulin; prefect Mao Jiong crushed him, beheading Wu’s inspector of Jiao, Liu Jun, and general Xiu Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong of Wu invaded Yulin; Mao Jiong shattered his army and took the heads of Jiao inspector Liu Jun and general Xiu Ze.

sentences.zh: 十一月，吳將丁奉等出芍陂，安東將軍汝陰王駿與義陽王望擊走之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Wu generals including Ding Feng came out from Quepi; general who guards the east Sima Jun, king of Ru'yin, together with Sima Wang of Yiyang, drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: Ding Feng led Wu forces out of Quepi; Sima Jun and Sima Wang threw them back.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔王公卿尹及郡國守相，舉賢良方正直言之士。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei an edict ordered kings, dukes, chief ministers, and commandery and principality governors and chiefs to recommend men worthy, good, and upright who spoke plainly.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei he called for nominations of worthy, honest, outspoken talent from every princely house and province.

sentences.zh: 十二月，班五條詔書於郡國：一曰正身，二曰勤百姓，三曰撫孤寡，四曰敦本息末，五曰去人事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the five-article edict was promulgated to commanderies and principalities: first, rectify oneself; second, diligently care for the hundred surnames; third, soothe widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary; fourth, stress the root and restrain the tip; fifth, remove private networking.
translations.idiomatic: December brought the five-point provincial charter—self-cultivation, care for the people, relief for the helpless, agriculture over commerce, and an end to clientage.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，帝臨聽訟觀，錄廷尉洛陽獄囚，親平決焉。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin the emperor attended the hall for hearing lawsuits, reviewed the prisoners of the commandant of justice at Luoyang, and personally settled their cases.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he sat in the Luoyang review court and personally cleared the capital jail.

sentences.zh: 扶南、林邑各遣使來獻。

translations.literal: Funan and Lin-yi each sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Funan and Lin-yi both dispatched embassies with gifts.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月癸巳，申戒郡國計吏守相令長，務盡地利，禁游食商販。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, spring, first month, on the day guisi, he sternly admonished the commandery accounting clerks, governors, and chiefs to exhaust the advantages of the soil and forbid vagrant peddlers.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, spring, guisi: account clerks and magistrates were warned to fill every acre and ban idle hawkers.

sentences.zh: 丙申，帝臨聽訟觀錄囚徒，多所原遣。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen the emperor attended the hall for hearing lawsuits, reviewed prisoners, and many were pardoned or released.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen he heard capital cases again and freed a large number.

sentences.zh: 青龍二見於滎陽。

translations.literal: Two azure dragons appeared at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Twin azure dragons were reported at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 二月，以雍州隴右五郡及涼州之金城、梁州之陰平置秦州。

translations.literal: In the second month Qin province was established from the five commanderies of Yongzhou west of the Long Range, together with Jincheng commandery from the northwest frontier and Yinping commandery from the Hanzhong uplands.
translations.idiomatic: That February he carved out Qin province, combining the five Longyou commanderies under Yong with Jincheng from the Hexi frontier and Yinping from the Hanzhong basin.

sentences.zh: [11]辛巳，白龍二見於趙國。

translations.literal: [11] On the day xinsi two white dragons were seen in the principality of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: [11] On xinsi two white dragons appeared in Zhao.

sentences.zh: 青、徐、兗三州水，遣使振恤之。

translations.literal: The provinces of Qing, Xu, and Yan suffered floods; envoys were sent to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Flooding struck Qing, Xu, and Yan; the court dispatched inspectors with grain and aid.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以尚書左僕射羊祜都督荊州諸軍事，征東大將軍衛瓘都督青州諸軍事，東莞王伷鎮東大將軍、都督徐州諸軍事。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Yang Hu, senior vice-director of the masters of the left, was appointed to supervise all military affairs of Jing province; Wei Guan, great general who campaigns east, was appointed to supervise all military affairs of Qing province; king Zhou of Dongguan was made great general who guards the east and supervisor of all military affairs of Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Yang Hu took command on the Jing front, Wei Guan on the Qing front, and Sima Zhou of Dongguan became commander-in-chief on the Xu front.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔曰：「古者歲書群吏之能否，三年而誅賞之。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai an edict said: “In antiquity the year’s record set down whether host of clerks could or could not perform their duties; after three years they were executed or rewarded.”
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he recalled the old rule of triennial review of every clerk’s fitness.

sentences.zh: 諸令史前後，但簡遣疏劣，而無有勸進，非黜陟之謂也。

translations.literal: Among the clerks of the various prefectures, hitherto only the slack and inferior were winnowed out and dismissed, while there was no encouragement of advancement—this is not what demotion and promotion mean.”
translations.idiomatic: So far prefects had only purged the useless without promoting the able—that was not true evaluation.

sentences.zh: 其條勤能有稱尤異者，歲以爲常。

translations.literal: Let those whose diligence and ability win praise as outstanding be recorded annually as a constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: Any clerk praised year after year for diligence and talent should be entered on a standing honor roll.

sentences.zh: 吾將議其功勞。

translations.literal: I shall deliberate their merit and labor.”
translations.idiomatic: The throne will then weigh rewards for proven service.”

sentences.zh: 」己未，[12]詔蜀相諸葛亮孫京隨才署吏。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei [12] an edict ordered that Sun Jing, grandson of Shu’s chancellor Zhuge Liang, be appointed to office according to his talents.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei [12] Zhuge Liang’s descendant Sun Jing was given a post suited to his abilities.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，地震。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month: the earth shook.

sentences.zh: 五月辛卯朔，鳳皇見于趙國。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, xinmao, a phoenix was seen in the principality of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month began on xinmao with a phoenix sighting in Zhao.

sentences.zh: 曲赦交趾、九真、日南五歲刑。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty remitted five years of penal labor in Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, and Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: The southern coast got a targeted pardon wiping five years of hard labor sentences.

sentences.zh: 六月，鄴奚官督郭廙上疏陳五事以諫，言甚切直，擢爲屯留令。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Guo Yi, overseer of Ye’s “Xi” artisans, submitted a memorial stating five points of remonstrance in very blunt terms; he was promoted to magistrate of Tunliu.
translations.idiomatic: A Ye workshop overseer named Guo Yi sent up a blunt five-point memorial and was rewarded with the Tunliu magistracy.

sentences.zh: 西平人麴路伐登聞鼓，言多祅謗，有司奏棄市。

translations.literal: A man of Xiping, Qu Lu, beat the drum for hearing grievances and spoke much slanderous prophecy; the offices memorialized to execute him in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Lu of Xiping pounded the appeal drum with wild, slanderous talk; the ministry sought a public execution.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕之過也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “This is my fault.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered, “The fault is mine.”

sentences.zh: 」捨而不問。

translations.literal: He released Qu Lu and made no further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He let the man go without punishment.

sentences.zh: 罷鎮軍將軍，復置左右將軍官。

translations.literal: The general who guards the army was abolished, and posts of generals of the left and right were restored.
translations.idiomatic: The “guard the army” command was cut while left and right generals returned to the table of organization.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，延群公，詢讜言。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, he extended audience to the host of dukes and sought out candid counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: he convened the great nobles and asked for plain speech.

sentences.zh: 九月，有星孛于紫宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month a broom star appeared in the Purple Palace constellation.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: a comet blazed through the circumpolar palace.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙子，以汲郡太守王宏有政績，賜穀千斛。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day bingzi, because Wang Hong, prefect of Ji commandery, had administrative achievements, he was granted one thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, bingzi: Wang Hong of Ji won a thousand-hu bounty for good governance.

sentences.zh: 十一月，追封諡皇弟兆爲城陽哀王，以皇子景度嗣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he posthumously enfeoffed and gave a posthumous name to the imperial younger brother Zhao as king Ai of Chengyang, and the imperial son Jingdu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: November canonized the late prince Zhao as king Ai of Chengyang and installed Prince Jingdu in his line.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔州郡舉勇猛秀異之才。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he ordered commanderies and provinces to recommend men brave, fierce, and outstanding in talent.
translations.idiomatic: December: every province was told to nominate bold and exceptional warriors.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月丁亥朔，帝臨軒，不設樂。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, spring, first month, on the first day dinghai, the emperor came to the gallery; music was not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 6, new year on dinghai: he held court in the gallery without music.

sentences.zh: 吳將丁奉入渦口，揚州刺史牽弘擊走之。

translations.literal: Wu general Ding Feng entered the mouth of the Wo River; Qian Hong, inspector of Yang province, attacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Feng of Wu probed the Wo estuary until Qian Hong, Yang’s inspector, threw him back.

sentences.zh: 三月，赦五歲刑已下。

translations.literal: In the third month he pardoned penal labor up to five years.
translations.idiomatic: Third month: sentences of five years or less were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，白龍二見於東莞。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, two white dragons were seen at Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Summer: twin white dragons were reported in Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 五月，立壽安亭侯承爲南宮王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he established Cheng, marquis of the village of Shou'an, as king of the southern palace.
translations.idiomatic: May raised marquis Cheng of Shou'an village to king of the southern palace.

sentences.zh: 六月戊午，秦州刺史胡烈擊叛虜於萬斛堆，力戰，死之。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu of the sixth month, Hu Lie, inspector of Qin province, attacked mutinous tribesmen at Wanhudui, fought hard, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, wuwu: Hu Lie died charging tribal rebels at Wanhudui.

sentences.zh: 詔遣尚書石鑒行安西將軍、都督秦州諸軍事，與奮威護軍田章討之。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched supervisor of the masters of writing Shi Jian to act as general who pacifies the west and supervise all military affairs of Qin province, together with protector general who displays might Tian Zhang to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian was sent west as acting pacification general with Tian Zhang’s vanguard to crush the rising.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁酉，復隴右五郡遇寇害者租賦，不能自存者廩貸之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day dingyou, land tax and labor surtax were remitted for the five Longyou commanderies that had suffered bandit harm, and those unable to support themselves were loaned grain from the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, dingyou: the five Longyou counties ravaged by raiders were tax-free, and starving households got grain loans.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，城陽王景度薨。

translations.literal: On the day yisi king Jingdu of Chengyang died.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the young king of Chengyang, Jingdu, died.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自泰始以來，大事皆撰錄祕書，寫副。

translations.literal: An edict said: “Since Taishi, great affairs have all been compiled in the secretariat with duplicate copies written.”
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that every major state paper since Taishi stay on file in the palace archive with a fair copy.

sentences.zh: 後有其事，輒宜綴集以爲常。

translations.literal: Whenever later there is such an affair, it should at once be appended and gathered as a constant practice.”
translations.idiomatic: Future events of the same weight must be added to the dossier as routine.”

sentences.zh: 」丁未，以汝陰王駿爲鎮西大將軍、都督雍涼二州諸軍事。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei king Jun of Ru'yin was made great general who guards the west and supervisor of all military affairs of Yong and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Sima Jun of Ru'yin became western commander over Yong and Liang.

sentences.zh: 九月，大宛獻汗血馬，焉耆來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Ferghana presented sweat-blood horses, and Yanqi came to offer local tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Ferghana sent blood-sweating steeds; Yanqi sent envoys with gifts.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，幸辟雍，行鄉飲酒之禮，賜太常博士、學生帛牛酒各有差。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month he visited the Biyong academy, performed the village drinking rite, and bestowed silks, oxen, and wine on the grand master of ceremonies’ erudits and students, each according to scale.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, eleventh month: at the imperial academy he held the archery feast and handed out silk, beef, and wine to ritual scholars and students by rank.

sentences.zh: 立皇子柬爲汝南王。

translations.literal: He established the imperial son Jian as king of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian was named king of Runan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，吳夏口督、前將軍孫秀帥眾來奔，拜驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，封會稽公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Sun Xiu, Wu’s commander at Xiakou and former forward general, led his troops to defect; he was appointed general of swift cavalry with independent command equal to the three excellencies and enfeoffed as duke of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: December: Sun Xiu, Wu’s Xiakou commander, defected with his army and received a ducal title and swift-cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，復置鎮軍官。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen the post of general who guards the army was restored.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the “guard the army” office was revived.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月丙午，皇太子冠，賜王公以下帛各有差。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, spring, first month, on the day bingwu, the crown prince underwent the capping ceremony; silks were bestowed on the kings and dukes downward, each according to scale.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, bingwu: the heir was capped and nobles down the line got graded silk gifts.

sentences.zh: 匈奴帥劉猛叛出塞。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu leader Liu Meng rebelled and went out beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain Liu Meng broke with the court and fled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 三月，孫皓帥眾趨壽陽，遣大司馬望屯淮北以距之。

translations.literal: In the third month Sun Hao led his host toward Shouyang; the grand marshal Wang was sent to encamp north of the Huai to block him.
translations.idiomatic: Third month: Sun Hao marched on Shouyang; grand marshal Sima Wang took station north of the Huai to meet him.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，[13]司空、鉅鹿公裴秀薨。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu [13] Pei Xiu, minister of works and duke of Julu, died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu [13] Pei Xiu, minister of works, died.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以中護軍王業爲尚書左僕射，高陽王珪爲尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day guisi Wang Ye, central protector, was appointed senior vice-director of the masters of the left, and king Gui of Gaoyang senior vice-director of the masters of the right.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Wang Ye and Sima Gui were paired as left and right vice-presidents of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孫秀部將何崇帥眾五千人來降。
