translations.literal: In the seventh year, spring, first month, on the first day jiayin, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 7, jiayin: eclipse.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔曰：「比年災異屢發，日蝕三朝，地震山崩。

translations.literal: On the day yimao an edict said: “In recent years omens have repeatedly appeared—three court mornings with solar eclipses, earthquakes and mountain collapses.”
translations.idiomatic: Yimao: the emperor blamed himself for eclipses and quakes.

sentences.zh: 邦之不臧，實在朕躬。

translations.literal: When the state is not good, the fault is truly in my person.”
translations.idiomatic: When the realm falters, the blame lies with me alone.”

sentences.zh: 公卿大臣各上封事，極言其故，勿有所諱。」

translations.literal: Let each duke and minister submit a sealed memorial, speaking to the utmost of the reasons, and let none hold back.”
translations.idiomatic: I want sealed memorials from every minister, candid and complete.”

sentences.zh: 夏五月，郡國十三旱。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, thirteen commanderies and principalities had drought.
translations.idiomatic: Summer drought gripped thirteen provinces.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑慕容廆寇遼東。

translations.literal: Murong Hui of the Xianbei raided Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui struck Liaodong again.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，朱提山崩，犍爲地震。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month Mount Zhuti collapsed and Qianwei suffered an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: Zhuti mountain fell and Qianwei shook.

sentences.zh: 八月，東夷十一國內附。

translations.literal: In the eighth month eleven states of the eastern Yi submitted within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: August: eleven Yi peoples asked to join Jin.

sentences.zh: 京兆地震。

translations.literal: Jingzhao suffered an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: The capital region trembled.

sentences.zh: 九月戊寅，驃騎將軍、扶風王駿薨。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin of the ninth month Sima Jun, swift-cavalry general and king of Fufeng, died.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyin: Sima Jun of Fufeng died.

sentences.zh: 郡國八大水。

translations.literal: Eight commanderies and principalities had great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Eight provinces flooded.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月壬子，以隴西王泰都督關中諸軍事。

translations.literal: On the day renzi of winter, eleventh month, king Tai of Longxi was appointed supervisor of all military affairs within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Renzi: Sima Tai took command of Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣侍御史巡遭水諸郡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month investigating censors were dispatched to tour commanderies that had suffered flood.
translations.idiomatic: Censors toured flood-hit counties with relief mandates.

sentences.zh: 出後宮才人、妓女以下二百七十人歸于家。

translations.literal: Two hundred seventy women from talented ladies and singing-girls downward in the rear palace were sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred seventy palace women of lower rank were freed to marry out.

sentences.zh: 始制大臣聽終喪三年。

translations.literal: It was first decreed that great ministers might observe the full three-year mourning for parents.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time chief ministers could sit the full three-year parent funeral.

sentences.zh: 己亥，河陰雨赤雪二頃。

translations.literal: On the day jihai crimson snow fell for two qing in Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Jihai: red snow covered two qing at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 是歲，扶南等二十一國、馬韓等十一國遣使來獻。

translations.literal: That year twenty-one states including Funan and eleven including Ma Han sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one southern and eleven Korean-style states sent embassies.

sentences.zh: 八年春正月戊申朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, spring, first month, on the first day wushen, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 8, wushen: eclipse.

sentences.zh: 太廟殿陷。

translations.literal: The hall of the grand ancestral temple collapsed inward.
translations.idiomatic: The great temple’s main hall fell in.

sentences.zh: 三月乙丑，臨商觀震。

translations.literal: On the day yichou of the third month the Shangguan observation tower was shaken by an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, yichou: the Shangguan watchtower rocked in a tremor.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，齊國、天水隕霜，[37]傷麥。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Qi principality and Tianshui had killing frost [37] that injured the wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Summer frost [37] ruined wheat in Qi and Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 六月，魯國大風，拔樹木，壞百姓廬舍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Lu principality had great wind that uprooted trees and ruined commoners’ huts.
translations.idiomatic: June gales in Lu tore up forests and homes.

sentences.zh: 郡國八大水。

translations.literal: Eight commanderies and principalities had great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Eight provinces flooded again.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，前殿地陷，深數丈，中有破船。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the ground before the front hall collapsed several zhang deep, and within was a broken boat.
translations.idiomatic: The front hall yard opened into a pit revealing an ancient wreck.

sentences.zh: 八月，東夷二國內附。

translations.literal: In the eighth month two states of the eastern Yi submitted within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Two more Yi groups enrolled.

sentences.zh: 九月，改營太廟。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the grand temple was ordered rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: September: plans to rebuild the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，南康平固縣吏李豐反，聚眾攻郡縣，自號將軍。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month clerk Li Feng of Pinggu county in Nankang rebelled, gathered a crowd, attacked commanderies and counties, and styled himself general.
translations.idiomatic: Winter: Li Feng’s mutiny in southern Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 十一月，海安令蕭輔聚眾反。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Xiao Fu, magistrate of Hai’an, gathered a crowd and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: November: Xiao Fu rose at Hai’an.

sentences.zh: 十二月，吳興人蔣迪聚黨反，圍陽羨縣，州郡捕討，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jiang Di of Wu-xing gathered a party, rebelled, besieged Yangxian county, and was hunted down by province and commandery; all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: December: Jiang Di’s band in Wu-xing was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 南夷扶南、西域康居國各遣使來獻。

translations.literal: Funan in the southern Yi and Kangju in the Western Regions each sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Funan and Kangju sent embassies.

sentences.zh: 是歲，郡國五地震。

translations.literal: That year five commanderies and principalities suffered earthquakes.
translations.idiomatic: Five provinces reported quakes.

sentences.zh: 九年春正月壬申朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, spring, first month, on the first day renshen, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 9, renshen: eclipse.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「興化之本，由政平訟理也。

translations.literal: An edict said: “The root of promoting transformation lies in even government and balanced lawsuits.”
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed that honest justice is the basis of good rule.

sentences.zh: 二千石長吏不能勤恤人隱，而輕挾私故，興長刑獄，又多貪濁，煩撓百姓。

translations.literal: Governors at two thousand piculs and chiefs who cannot diligently pity the people’s hardships, but lightly indulge private reasons, thereby prolonging litigation, and who moreover are mostly greedy and corrupt, vexing the hundred surnames—
translations.idiomatic: He scolded magistrates who pile up cases for private gain and bleed the people.

sentences.zh: 其敕刺史二千石糾其穢濁，舉其公清，有司議其黜陟。

translations.literal: order the inspectors and two-thousand-picul men to impeach their filth, praise their fairness and purity, and let the offices deliberate their demotion or promotion.”
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors must expose the corrupt and lift the clean for central review.”

sentences.zh: 令內外群官舉清能，拔寒素。

translations.literal: Order civil and military officials within and without to recommend the pure and capable and to raise men of cold and humble background.”
translations.idiomatic: Every office must nominate honest talent from poor families.”

sentences.zh: 」江東四郡地震。

translations.literal: There was an earthquake in the four commanderies east of the Yangzi River.
translations.idiomatic: The lower Yangzi region shook in four counties.

sentences.zh: 二月，尚書右僕射、陽夏侯胡奮卒，以尚書朱整爲尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second month Hu Fen, senior vice-director of the masters of the right and marquis of Yangxia, died; Zhu Zheng of the masters of writing was appointed senior vice-director of the masters of the right.
translations.idiomatic: February: Hu Fen died; Zhu Zheng took his secretariat seat.

sentences.zh: 三月丁丑，皇后親桑于西郊，賜帛各有差。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou of the third month the empress personally tended silkworms in the western suburb; silks were bestowed each according to difference.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchou: the empress held the silkworm rite and gifts followed.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，初并二社爲一。

translations.literal: On the day renchen the two soil altars were first merged into one.
translations.idiomatic: Renchen: the paired earth gods were combined in one rite.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，江南郡國八地震；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, eight commanderies and principalities south of the Yangzi suffered earthquakes;
translations.idiomatic: Summer: eight south-of-river counties shook;

sentences.zh: 隴西隕霜，傷宿麥。

translations.literal: Longxi had killing frost that injured the winter wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi frost killed the winter wheat.

sentences.zh: 五月，義陽王奇有罪，黜爲三縱亭侯。

translations.literal: In the fifth month king Qi of Yiyang committed a crime and was degraded to marquis of Sanzongting.
translations.idiomatic: May: Sima Qi of Yiyang lost his kingship for crime, becoming village marquis of Sanzongting.

sentences.zh: 詔內外群官舉守令之才。

translations.literal: An edict ordered civil and military officials within and without each to recommend men with talent to be shepherds and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: The court called for nominations of worthy prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 六月庚子朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, gengzi, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, new moon gengzi: eclipse.

sentences.zh: 徙章武王威爲義陽王。

translations.literal: King Wei of Zhangwu was transferred to be king of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Wei moved from Zhangwu to Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 郡國三十二大旱，傷麥。

translations.literal: Thirty-two commanderies and principalities suffered great drought that injured the wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-two provinces baked in drought that withered the wheat crop.

sentences.zh: 秋八月壬子，星隕如雨。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on the day renzi, stars fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, renzi: a meteor shower lit the sky.

sentences.zh: 詔郡國五歲刑以下決遣，無留庶獄。

translations.literal: An edict ordered commanderies and principalities to dispose of penal cases up to five years’ labor and not to leave common lawsuits detained.
translations.idiomatic: He told magistrates to clear dockets of minor sentences and end jail backlog.

sentences.zh: 九月，東夷七國詣校尉內附。

translations.literal: In the ninth month seven states of the eastern Yi came to the colonel and submitted within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Seven Yi peoples reported to the frontier colonel and enrolled as subjects.

sentences.zh: 郡國二十四螟。

translations.literal: Twenty-four commanderies and principalities suffered from grain-eating caterpillars.
translations.idiomatic: Crop-worms blighted twenty-four provinces.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月癸卯，立河間平王洪子英爲章武王。

translations.literal: On the day guimao of winter, twelfth month, Ying, son of king Hong the peaceful of Hejian, was established as king of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Guimao: Ying, son of Hejian’s Prince Hong, became king of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: [38]戊申，青龍、黃龍各一見于魯國。

translations.literal: [38] On the day wushen an azure dragon and a yellow dragon were each seen in Lu principality.
translations.idiomatic: [38] Wushen: one blue and one yellow dragon sighted in Lu.

sentences.zh: 十年夏四月，以京兆太守劉霄、陽平太守梁柳有政績，各賜穀千斛。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month of the tenth year, because Jingzhao prefect Liu Xiao and Yangping prefect Liang Liu had administrative achievements, each was granted one thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 10, summer: Liu Xiao and Liang Liu each won a thousand-hu bounty for good rule.

sentences.zh: 郡國八隕霜。

translations.literal: Eight commanderies and principalities had killing frost.
translations.idiomatic: Black frost struck eight provinces.

sentences.zh: 太廟成。

translations.literal: The grand ancestral temple was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The new imperial temple stood finished.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，遷神主于新廟，帝迎于道左，遂祫祭。

translations.literal: On the day yisi the spirit tablets were moved to the new temple; the emperor welcomed them on the left of the road, then performed the joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Yisi: ancestral tablets entered the new shrine in a procession the emperor met in person, followed by a combined offering.

sentences.zh: 大赦，文武增位一等，作廟者二等。

translations.literal: A great amnesty was declared; civil and military officials were advanced one grade in rank, and those who built the temple two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty came with promotions—one step for officials, two for temple builders.

sentences.zh: 丁未，尚書右僕射、廣興侯朱整卒。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei Zhu Zheng, senior vice-director of the masters of the right and marquis of Guangxing, died.
translations.idiomatic: Dingwei: Zhu Zheng died.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，崇賢殿災。

translations.literal: On the day guichou the Chongxian hall caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: Guichou: fire consumed the Chongxian hall.

sentences.zh: 五月，鮮卑慕容廆來降，東夷十一國內附。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Murong Hui of the Xianbei came to surrender, and eleven states of the eastern Yi submitted within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: May: Murong Hui yielded while eleven Yi realms joined Jin.

sentences.zh: 六月庚子，山陽公劉瑾薨。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi of the sixth month Liu Jin, mountain-yang duke, died.
translations.idiomatic: Gengzi: Liu Jin, mountain-yang duke, died.

sentences.zh: 復置二社。

translations.literal: The two soil altars were restored.
translations.idiomatic: The paired earth-god altars were reinstated.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬子，徙南宮王承爲武邑王。

translations.literal: On the day renzi of winter, tenth month, king Cheng of the southern palace was transferred to be king of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Renzi: the southern-palace king became prince of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙辰，守尚書令、左光祿大夫荀勖卒。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen of the eleventh month Xun Xu, acting supervisor of the masters of writing and grand officer of the left brilliance, died.
translations.idiomatic: Bingchen: Xun Xu died in office.

sentences.zh: 帝疾瘳，賜王公以下帛有差。

translations.literal: When the emperor’s illness abated, silks were bestowed on the kings and dukes downward, each according to difference.
translations.idiomatic: On partial recovery he handed out graded silk to the nobility.

sentences.zh: 含章殿鞠室火。

translations.literal: The ball-court chamber in the Hanzhang hall caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: Fire broke out in the Hanzhang hall’s indoor ball court.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以汝南王亮爲大司馬、大都督、假黃鉞。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen Sima Liang, king of Runan, was appointed grand marshal, supreme commander, and given the yellow axe as credential.
translations.idiomatic: Jiashen: Sima Liang became grand marshal and supreme commander with the yellow axe.

sentences.zh: 改封南陽王柬爲秦王，始平王瑋爲楚王，濮陽王允爲淮南王，並假節之國，各統方州軍事。

translations.literal: King Jian of Nanyang was transferred to be king of Qin, king Wei of Shiping to king of Chu, king Yun of Puyang to king of Huainan, each bearing the staff of authority to his state and commanding regional military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Three princes were sent out with full powers—Jian to Qin, Wei to Chu, Yun to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 立皇子乂爲長沙王，穎爲成都王，晏爲吳王，熾爲豫章王，演爲代王，皇孫遹爲廣陵王。

translations.literal: He established the imperial son Yi as king of Changsha, Ying as king of Chengdu, Yan as king of Wu, Chi as king of Yuzhang, Yan as king of Dai, and the imperial grandson Yu as king of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: A ring of younger sons and the heir’s son received kingdoms from Changsha to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 立濮陽王子迪爲漢王，始平王子儀爲毗陵王，汝南王次子羕爲西陽公。

translations.literal: He established Di, son of the king of Puyang, as king of Han; Yi, son of the king of Shiping, as king of Piling; Yang, second son of the king of Runan, as duke of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cadet lines were ennobled—Han, Piling, and Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 徙扶風王暢爲順陽王，暢弟歆爲新野公，琅邪王覲弟澹爲東武公，繇爲東安公，漼爲廣陵公，卷爲東莞公。

translations.literal: King Chang of Fufeng was transferred to be king of Shunyang; Xin, Chang’s younger brother, was made duke of Xinye; Dan, younger brother of king Jin of Langye, duke of Dongwu; You duke of Dong’an; Cui duke of Guangling; Juan duke of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: More kinsmen were shuffled—Chang to Shunyang, with younger brothers and cousins given lesser ducal seats.

sentences.zh: 改諸王國相爲內史。

translations.literal: The ministers of princely states were renamed interior historians.
translations.idiomatic: Princely “chancellors” became “interior historians.”

sentences.zh: 十二月庚寅，[39]太廟梁折。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin of the twelfth month [39] a beam in the grand temple broke.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyin [39]: a roof-beam cracked in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 是歲，東夷絕遠三十餘國、西南夷二十餘國來獻。

translations.literal: That year more than thirty distant eastern Yi states and more than twenty southwestern Yi states came to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Embassies arrived from thirty-plus eastern and twenty-plus southwestern tribes.

sentences.zh: 虜奚軻男女十萬口來降。

translations.literal: One hundred thousand persons, men and women, of the Xike tribe came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand Xike tribespeople submitted to Jin.

translations.literal: [40] The received text carries commentary marker [40] at this point.
translations.idiomatic: Manuscripts mark editorial note [40] here.

sentences.zh: 二月辛丑，東夷七國朝貢。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou of the second month seven eastern Yi states came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, xinchou: seven Yi missions at court.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王覲薨。

translations.literal: King Jin of Langye died.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Langye, Sima Jin, died.

sentences.zh: 三月甲子，以右光祿大夫石鑒爲司空。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi of the third month Shi Jian, grand officer of the right brilliance, was appointed minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazi: Shi Jian became minister of works.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛丑，以侍中車騎將軍楊駿爲太尉、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day xinchou, Yang Jun, palace attendant and general of chariots and cavalry, was appointed grand commandant, supervisor of all military affairs within and without, and recorder of masters-of-writing business.
translations.idiomatic: Xinchou: Yang Jun took the triple portfolio—grand commandant, commander-in-chief, and chief of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 己酉，帝崩于含章殿，時年五十五，葬峻陽陵，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou the emperor died in the Hanzhang hall at age fifty-five; he was buried at Junyang mausoleum with temple name Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyou: the emperor expired in Hanzhang at fifty-five, resting as Shizu at Junyang.

sentences.zh: 帝宇量弘厚，造次必於仁恕；

translations.literal: The emperor’s bearing was broad and his capacity magnanimous; even in haste he acted with benevolence and forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: He was large-spirited and humane even under pressure.

sentences.zh: 容納讜正，未嘗失色於人；

translations.literal: He accepted blunt counsel and never showed anger on his face toward others.
translations.idiomatic: He heard hard truths without losing his temper.

sentences.zh: 明達善謀，能斷大事，故得撫寧萬國，綏靜四方。

translations.literal: He was perspicacious, skilled in planning, and able to decide great matters, and therefore could soothe and stabilize the myriad regions and bring quiet to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: His judgment pacified the realm.

sentences.zh: 承魏氏奢侈刻弊之後，百姓思古之遺風，乃厲以恭儉，敦以寡慾。

translations.literal: Following the Wei dynasty’s extravagance and harsh exactions, the hundred surnames longed for the surviving air of antiquity; he therefore enforced reverence and frugality and pressed for few desires.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei’s luxury and cruelty, he modeled austerity and restraint.

sentences.zh: 有司嘗奏御牛青絲紖斷，詔以青麻代之。

translations.literal: Once the offices memorialized that the imperial ox’s blue silk halter had snapped; he ordered hemp substituted.
translations.idiomatic: When clerks noted the palace ox’s silk lead had broken, he told them to use hemp instead.

sentences.zh: 臨朝寬裕，法度有恆。

translations.literal: In court he was lenient and law and measure remained constant.
translations.idiomatic: His sessions were calm and the code steady.

sentences.zh: 高陽許允既爲文帝所殺，允子奇爲太常丞。

translations.literal: Xu Yun of Gaoyang had already been killed by emperor Wen; Yun’s son Qi served as assistant director of the grand master of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun, whom Wen had executed, left a son Qi in the ritual office.

sentences.zh: 帝將有事於太廟，朝議以奇受害之門，不欲接近左右，請出爲長史。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to perform business in the grand temple, court discussion held that Qi came from a house that had suffered harm and should not be kept near the throne, requesting he be sent out as senior clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers wanted Qi barred from the rite as a victim’s son.

sentences.zh: 帝乃追述允夙望，稱奇之才，擢爲祠部郎，時論稱其夷曠。

translations.literal: The emperor then recalled Xu Yun’s old repute, praised Qi’s talent, promoted him to director in the sacrifices bureau, and opinion of the time praised his fairness and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor overruled them, praised Qi, and raised him—critics called it magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 平吳之後，天下乂安，遂怠於政術，耽於遊宴，寵愛后黨，親貴當權，舊臣不得專任，彝章紊廢，請謁行矣。

translations.literal: After Wu was pacified, all under heaven was at peace; thereupon he slackened in governing methods, indulged in roaming feasts, doted on the empress’s kin, let close nobles hold power, no longer gave old ministers sole responsibility, canonical regulations fell into disorder, and soliciting favor became the way.
translations.idiomatic: Peace bred complacency: harem kin and favorites took the reins while law grew slack.

sentences.zh: 爰至末年，知惠帝弗克負荷，然恃皇孫聰睿，故無廢立之心。

translations.literal: By his last years he knew that emperor Hui could not bear the burden, yet he trusted in the imperial grandson’s cleverness and therefore had no mind to change the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he saw Hui’s weakness but pinned hope on a bright grandson.

sentences.zh: 復慮非賈后所生，終致危敗，遂與腹心共圖後事。

translations.literal: He again feared that because the child was not born of empress Jia, disaster would ultimately follow, and therefore plotted the aftermath with his intimates.
translations.idiomatic: He worried Jia’s lack of maternity would doom the line and schemed with confidants.

sentences.zh: 說者紛然，久而不定，竟用王佑之謀，遣太子母弟秦王柬都督關中，楚王瑋、淮南王允並鎮守要害，以強帝室。

translations.literal: Opinions flew thick and long without settlement; in the end he adopted Wang You’s plan, sending the crown prince’s younger uterine brother, king Jian of Qin, to command Guanzhong, while kings Wei of Chu and Yun of Huainan jointly guarded critical points to strengthen the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: He settled on Wang You’s scheme—princely armies on key frontiers to prop the throne.

sentences.zh: 又恐楊氏之偪，復以佑爲北軍中候，以典禁兵。

translations.literal: Fearing pressure from the Yang clan, he again made Wang You inspector of the northern armies to command the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: To check the Yangs he gave Wang You the northern-army baton.

sentences.zh: 既而寢疾彌留，至於大漸，佐命元勳，皆已先沒，群臣惶惑，計無所從。

translations.literal: Soon he lay gravely ill; as he approached the final crisis, the founding ministers had all predeceased him, and the host of officials were frightened and at a loss.
translations.idiomatic: When death neared, his great generals were gone and the court panicked.

sentences.zh: 會帝小差，有詔以汝南王亮輔政，又欲令朝士之有名望年少者數人佐之，楊駿祕而不宣。

translations.literal: When the emperor briefly improved, an edict ordered king Liang of Runan to assist the government, and he also wished to have several young courtiers of high repute assist him, but Yang Jun suppressed the edict and did not proclaim it.
translations.idiomatic: A brief rally produced orders for Sima Liang and young worthies—Yang Jun hid the edict.

sentences.zh: 帝復尋至迷亂，楊后輒爲詔以駿輔政，促亮進發。

translations.literal: The emperor relapsed into confusion; empress Yang then forged an edict making Yang Jun regent and urging Liang to hurry to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang forged a regency for Yang Jun.

sentences.zh: 帝尋小間，問汝南王來未，意欲見之，有所付託。

translations.literal: The emperor briefly cleared and asked whether the king of Runan had arrived, intending to see him and entrust something.
translations.idiomatic: In a lucid moment he asked for Sima Liang.

sentences.zh: 左右答言未至，帝遂困篤。

translations.literal: Those at his side answered that he had not yet arrived, and the emperor thereupon sank into critical illness.
translations.idiomatic: Told Liang had not come, he sank back into coma.

sentences.zh: 中朝之亂，實始於斯矣。

translations.literal: The turmoil at court truly began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The mid-realm disasters trace to this bedside failure.

sentences.zh: 制曰：武皇承基，誕膺天命，握圖御宇，敷化導民，以佚代勞，以治易亂。

translations.literal: The official rescript states: The Martial Emperor received the foundation, truly bore heaven’s mandate, grasped the chart and ruled the realm, spread transformation and guided the people, replacing toil with ease and exchanging chaos for order.
translations.idiomatic: The court’s summation runs thus: Emperor Wu inherited the enterprise, claimed Heaven’s charge, mastered the realm’s map, and turned exhaustion and disorder into rest and rule.

sentences.zh: 絕縑綸之貢，去雕琢之飾，制奢俗以變儉約，止澆風而反淳朴。

translations.literal: He cut off the tribute of fine silks, removed carved and polished ornament, curbed extravagant custom toward frugality, and checked dissolute winds to return to simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: He banned luxury tribute and chased the court back toward plain living.

sentences.zh: 雅好直言，留心采擢，劉毅、裴楷以質直見容，嵇紹、許奇雖仇讎不棄。

translations.literal: He loved straight words and attended to selection; Liu Yi and Pei Kai were tolerated for blunt honesty, Ji Shao and Xu Qi were not cast aside though they were sons of enemies.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed Liu Yi, Pei Kai, Ji Shao, and Xu Qi despite awkward pedigrees.

sentences.zh: 仁以御物，寬而得眾，宏略大度，有帝王之量焉。

translations.literal: With kindness he governed things, with leniency he won the multitude; he had grand strategy and large tolerance—the measure of a true emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with humane breadth worthy of a founder.

sentences.zh: 於時民和俗靜，家給人足，聿修武用，思啟封疆。

translations.literal: At that time the people were harmonious and customs quiet, households had enough and persons sufficed; he repaired military readiness and thought to open the frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: The realm prospered while he sharpened the sword for expansion.

sentences.zh: 決神算於深衷，斷雄圖於議表。

translations.literal: He settled divine calculations in his secret heart and cut heroic plans from memorial debate.
translations.idiomatic: He decided great strategy in council and in his own mind.

sentences.zh: 馬隆西伐，王濬南征，師不延時，獯虜削跡，兵無血刃，揚越爲墟。

translations.literal: Ma Long campaigned west; Wang Jun marched south—the armies did not tarry, the savage tribes were erased, blades scarcely drew blood, and Yang and Yue became wastes.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long and Wang Jun finished the frontier and the south without prolonged war.

sentences.zh: 通上代之不通，服前王之未服。

translations.literal: He opened what former ages could not open and submitted what former kings had not submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He finished what past dynasties could not.

sentences.zh: 禎祥顯應，風教肅清，天人之功成矣，霸王之業大矣。

translations.literal: Auspicious omens responded clearly, wind and instruction were sternly pure; the merit of heaven and man was achieved, the enterprise of hegemon-king was great.
translations.idiomatic: Omens and morale alike proclaimed a golden age.

sentences.zh: 雖登封之禮，讓而不爲，驕泰之心，因斯以起。

translations.literal: Although he yielded and did not perform the Mount Tai enfeoffment rite, a mind of pride and ease arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: He modestly skipped the Feng sacrifice yet grew complacent.

sentences.zh: 見土地之廣，謂萬葉而無虞；

translations.literal: Seeing the breadth of the land, he supposed myriad generations would need no caution;
translations.idiomatic: He mistook vast territory for perpetual safety;

sentences.zh: 睹天下之安，謂千年而永治。

translations.literal: beholding the peace of the realm, he thought a thousand years of good order assured.
translations.idiomatic: he mistook quiet rule for an eternal guarantee.

sentences.zh: 不知處廣以思狹，則廣可長廣；

translations.literal: He did not know that dwelling in breadth while thinking of narrow straits can keep breadth long broad;
translations.idiomatic: Breadth lasts only if one remembers how easily it narrows;

sentences.zh: 居治而忘危，則治無常治。

translations.literal: that sitting in order while forgetting peril means order is not constant order.
translations.idiomatic: peace lasts only if peril stays in mind.

sentences.zh: 加之建立非所，委寄失才，志欲就於升平，行先迎於禍亂。

translations.literal: Add to this that establishment was not in the right place, commissions missed the right men—his aim sought rising peace, yet his acts first invited calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Wrong heirs and wrong ministers turned pursuit of stability into invitation to chaos.

sentences.zh: 是猶將適越者指沙漠以遵途，欲登山者涉舟航而覓路，所趣逾遠，所尚轉難，南北倍殊，高下相反，求其至也，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: It is like one who would go to Yue pointing at the desert for a road, or one who would climb a mountain crossing by boat to seek a path—the goal grows farther, the object harder, south and north doubly wrong, high and low reversed; to seek arrival—is it not hard!
translations.idiomatic: His choices were as absurd as sailing to a mountaintop.

sentences.zh: 況以新集易動之基，而無久安難拔之慮，故賈充凶豎，懷姦志以擁權；

translations.literal: Moreover, on a newly gathered, easily shaken base, without long-term plans against stubborn peril, therefore Jia Chong, a vicious fellow, harbored treachery and clutched power;
translations.idiomatic: On shaky foundations Jia Chong hoarded authority;

sentences.zh: 楊駿豺狼，苞禍心以專輔。

translations.literal: Yang Jun, a jackal-wolf, wrapped a baleful heart and monopolized assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun seized the regency with predatory intent.

sentences.zh: 及乎宮車晚出，諒闇未周，藩翰變親以成疏，連兵競滅其本；

translations.literal: When at last the palace coach departed late and the mourning curtains had not yet completed their round, the screen princes turned kin into strangers and linked armies to destroy their own root;
translations.idiomatic: Before the tomb closed, princely armies turned on one another;

sentences.zh: 棟梁回忠而起僞，擁眾各舉其威。

translations.literal: beams and pillars turned loyalty into treachery and each raised hosts to vaunt his might.
translations.idiomatic: Former pillars of state feigned loyalty while raising private armies.

sentences.zh: 曾未數年，綱紀大亂，海內版蕩，宗廟播遷。

translations.literal: In not a few years the great net was wildly tangled, the seas within the passes were in turmoil, and the ancestral temples were driven to flight.
translations.idiomatic: Within years the realm shattered and the altars fled.

sentences.zh: 帝道王猷，反居文身之俗；

translations.literal: Imperial way and kingly norm fell among folk who tattoo their bodies;
translations.idiomatic: Civilization collapsed into barbarous custom;

sentences.zh: 神州赤縣，翻成被髮之鄉。

translations.literal: the divine land of red counties overturned into a realm of disheveled hair.
translations.idiomatic: the heartland became a steppe frontier.

sentences.zh: 棄所大以資人，掩其小而自託，爲天下笑，其故何哉﹖良由失慎於前，所以貽患於後。

translations.literal: He cast aside what was great to enrich others, covered what was small and trusted to it—was he not laughed at by the world? The reason is truly that losing caution earlier planted calamity later.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away the store and became history’s cautionary tale.

sentences.zh: 且知子者賢父，知臣者明君；

translations.literal: Moreover, he who knows a son is a worthy father; he who knows a minister is an enlightened lord.
translations.idiomatic: The wise father knows his son, the wise ruler his minister;

sentences.zh: 子不肖則家亡，臣不忠則國亂；

translations.literal: If a son is not worthy the house perishes; if a minister is not loyal the state is in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Bad sons ruin families, disloyal ministers ruin states;

sentences.zh: 國亂不可以安也，家亡不可以全也。

translations.literal: A state in chaos cannot be made tranquil; a house perishing cannot be kept whole.
translations.idiomatic: Neither state nor house survives that rot.

sentences.zh: 是以君子防其始，聖人閑其端。

translations.literal: Therefore the gentleman guards the beginning, the sage blocks the opening.
translations.idiomatic: The wise seal trouble at the source.

sentences.zh: 而世祖惑荀勖之姦謀，迷王渾之僞策，心屢移於眾口，事不定於己圖。

translations.literal: Yet Shizu was deluded by Xun Xu’s treacherous counsel, misled by Wang Hun’s false strategy, his heart repeatedly swayed by many mouths, affairs unsettled by his own deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu listened to Xun Xu and Wang Hun and let rumor steer him.

sentences.zh: 元海當除而不除，卒令擾亂區夏；

translations.literal: Yuanhai ought to have been removed and was not removed, ultimately letting him disturb the central plain;
translations.idiomatic: He spared Liu Yuan and reaped rebellion;

sentences.zh: 惠帝可廢而不廢，終使傾覆洪基。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui could have been deposed and was not deposed, finally overturning the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a feeble heir and lost the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 夫全一人者德之輕，拯天下者功之重，棄一子者忍之小，安社稷者孝之大；

translations.literal: To preserve one man is a small virtue; to save the realm is a weighty merit; to cast off one child is a small hardness; to secure the altars is the great filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Saving the state outweighs sparing one prince;

sentences.zh: 況乎資三世而成業，延二孽以喪之，所謂取輕德而捨重功，畏小忍而忘大孝。

translations.literal: How much more when he had completed an enterprise through three reigns yet prolonged two baleful shoots to destroy it—what is called taking light virtue and discarding heavy merit, fearing small hardness and forgetting great filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: to waste three reigns’ work for two poisonous branches was to pick the lesser good.

sentences.zh: 聖賢之道，豈若斯乎！

translations.literal: Can the way of sages and worthies be like this!
translations.idiomatic: That is not the way of the sages.

sentences.zh: 雖則善始於初，而乖令終於末，所以殷勤史策，不能無慷慨焉。

translations.literal: Although he had a good beginning at first, he missed a fitting end at the last; therefore the histories linger here and cannot but sigh.
translations.idiomatic: A splendid start and a ruinous end invite the historian’s regret.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 子文爲沛王 李校：「宗室傳言沛王景字子文。

translations.literal: Regarding “Ziwen as king of Pei,” Li’s note: “The house-of-imperial-kin biography says the prince of Pei was named Jing with style Ziwen.”
translations.idiomatic: Li observes that the Pei prince was Jing, courtesy Ziwen.

sentences.zh: 此舉其字者，蓋沛王名本或作『炳』及『昞』、『秉』之類，唐避世祖諱昞，於『丙』、『秉』等字皆改爲『景』。

translations.literal: Here the style is given because the personal name was probably written Bing or similar characters later homogenized to Jing under Tang taboo on Bing for Shizu’s name.
translations.idiomatic: The annals use the style because Tang editors tabooed the true graph.

sentences.zh: 故紀稱其字，傳改爲『景』耳。

translations.literal: Hence the annals use his style while the biography reads Jing.”
translations.idiomatic: That is why the basic annals use the style.

sentences.zh: 」李說當是。

translations.literal: Li’s explanation should be correct.
translations.idiomatic: Li’s emendation stands.

sentences.zh: 鄉侯爲關內侯 「鄉侯」上原衍「爲」字，今刪。

translations.literal: Regarding “xiang marquises as marquises within the passes,” a superfluous wei was originally inserted above xiang hou; it is now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: A stray character before xiang hou has been removed per collation.

sentences.zh: 參拾補。

translations.literal: See the supplementary collation volume for details.
translations.idiomatic: Consult the addendum to the collation notes.

sentences.zh: 丁丑 二月己酉朔，丁丑爲二十九日，下文庚午爲二十二日，日序誤倒。

translations.literal: Regarding dingchou: second month begins jiyou new moon, so dingchou is the twenty-ninth day, while gengwu below is the twenty-second day—the day order is reversed in error.
translations.idiomatic: The stem-branch sequence is inconsistent in this month’s entries.

sentences.zh: 夏五月戊辰至壬子 舉正：五月無戊辰、壬子日。

translations.literal: Regarding “summer fifth month from wuchen to renzi”: the correction notes that fifth month has no wuchen or renzi days.
translations.idiomatic: The May date range is impossible as given.

sentences.zh: 春正月癸丑至丁卯 正月甲戌朔，無癸丑、丁卯。

translations.literal: Regarding spring first month from guichou to dingmao: first month begins jiaxu new moon, so neither guichou nor dingmao exists.
translations.idiomatic: The spring first-month span guichou–dingmao is impossible on the stated calendar.

sentences.zh: 丁未 三月癸酉朔，無丁未。

translations.literal: Regarding dingwei: third month begins guiyou new moon, so dingwei does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Dingwei cannot fall in that third month.

sentences.zh: 六月丙申朔 「丙申」，各本皆作「甲申」。

translations.literal: Regarding sixth month bingshen new moon: the text reads jiashen in all editions.
translations.idiomatic: Editions wrongly print jiashen where the almanac requires bingshen.

sentences.zh: 按：六月應爲丙申朔，丁國鈞晉書校文以下簡稱校文亦言「當從通鑑目錄作丙申」，今改正。

translations.literal: Comment: sixth month should begin on bingshen; Ding Guojun’s Jin shu collation (hereafter “Collation”) agrees with Zizhi tongjian’s calendar that bingshen is correct; emend accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars emend jiashen to bingshen per the Tongjian calendar.

sentences.zh: 戊午 七月丙寅朔，無戊午。

translations.literal: Regarding wuwu: seventh month begins bingyin new moon, so wuwu does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwu is absent from the seventh month’s stem-branch grid.

sentences.zh: 萬郁 斠注：「吳志三嗣主傳作『萬彧』。

translations.literal: Regarding Wan Yu: the collation note says Wu zhi, “Three Later Lords,” writes the name Wan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu annals give the graph Yu for this general’s name.

sentences.zh: 」按：通鑑七九同吳志。

translations.literal: Comment: Zizhi tongjian 79 follows Wu zhi in the same form.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongjian agrees with Wu zhi’s spelling.

sentences.zh: 梁州之陰平置秦州 「陰平」，各本皆作「陽平」。

translations.literal: Regarding “Yinping of Liangzhou to establish Qinzhou”: editions all read Yangping instead of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: Yangping is a common misprint for Yinping in this line.

sentences.zh: 商榷：「陽平，地理志作陰平，宜從之。

translations.literal: Discussion: the Treatise on Geography records Yinping; Yangping should be emended to Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: Geographers prefer Yinping; the text is corrected.

sentences.zh: 」今據改。

translations.literal: Therefore the text is emended on this evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The editors adopt Yinping.

sentences.zh: 己未 二月所見干支有辛巳、壬寅、丁亥、己未。

translations.literal: Regarding jiwei: the second month shows stems xinsi, renyin, dinghai, jiwei.
translations.idiomatic: February entries mix stems that spill into March.

sentences.zh: 按：二月壬戌朔，辛巳爲二十日，丁亥爲二十六日；

translations.literal: Comment: second month begins renxu new moon, so xinsi is the twentieth day and dinghai the twenty-sixth.
translations.idiomatic: Renxu opens February, fixing those two dates.

sentences.zh: 三月壬辰朔，壬寅爲十一日，己未爲二十八日。

translations.literal: Third month begins renchen new moon, so renyin is the eleventh day and jiwei the twenty-eighth.
translations.idiomatic: March opens on renchen, placing renyin and jiwei in the third month.

sentences.zh: 此處不見「三月」，且日序錯亂。

translations.literal: Here the text lacks “third month,” and the day order is confused.
translations.idiomatic: The annal omits the month head and scrambles chronology.

sentences.zh: 丙戌 「丙戌」上各本重出「三月」，今刪。

translations.literal: Regarding bingxu: editions duplicate “third month” above bingxu; delete the extra.
translations.idiomatic: Remove the repeated “third month” before bingxu.

sentences.zh: 辛酉 二月丁亥朔，無辛酉。

translations.literal: Regarding xinyou: second month begins dinghai new moon, so xinyou does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Xinyou cannot occur in that February.

sentences.zh: 參舉正。

translations.literal: See the “Rectification” section.
translations.idiomatic: See the collation rectification note.

sentences.zh: 六月癸丑至甲戌 六月庚辰朔，無癸丑、甲戌。

translations.literal: Regarding sixth month from guichou to jiaxu: sixth month begins gengchen new moon, so guichou and jiaxu do not exist.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth-month range guichou–jiaxu is impossible.

sentences.zh: 丁未起太倉於城東常平倉於東西市 九月戊申朔，無丁未。

translations.literal: Regarding dingwei raising the grand granary east of the city and ever-normal granaries in the eastern and western markets: ninth month begins wushen new moon, so dingwei does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Dingwei cannot fall in that ninth month.

sentences.zh: 本書食貨志及御覽一九〇引晉陽秋，謂泰始四年七月起常平倉。

translations.literal: This book’s Treatise on Food and Money and Taiping yulan 190’s quotation of Jin yangqiu say ever-normal granaries were founded in Taishi 4, seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Other sources date the granaries to Taishi 4/7.

sentences.zh: 平虜護軍文淑 周校：「扶風王駿、東安王繇傳並作『文俶』。

translations.literal: Regarding protector general who pacifies captives Wen Shu: Zhou’s collation notes that king Jun of Fufeng and king You of Dong’an both write the name Wen Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Parallel biographies use Wen Chu for the same man.

sentences.zh: 」按：魏志諸葛誕傳作「文鴦」，注引晉諸公贊又作「文俶」。

translations.literal: Comment: Wei zhi, Zhuge Dan’s biography, writes Wen Yang, while the commentary’s Jin zhugong zan again writes Wen Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao-Wei records alternate graphs Wen Yang and Wen Chu.

sentences.zh: 裴松之云鴦一名俶。

translations.literal: Pei Songzhi states that Yang is another name for Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi equates the two forms.

sentences.zh: 吳將邵凱 斠注：「羊祜傳『凱』作『顗』。

translations.literal: Regarding Wu general Shao Kai: the collation note says Yang Hu’s biography writes the second character as Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu’s memoir spells the name Shao Yi.

sentences.zh: 」按：通鑑八〇同祜傳。

translations.literal: Comment: Zizhi tongjian 80 follows Yang Hu’s form.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjian sides with Yang Hu’s spelling.

sentences.zh: 大風拔樹暴寒且冰 拾補：「五行志云河間，此上疑脫二字。

translations.literal: Regarding great wind uprooting trees, violent cold, and ice: the collation supplement says the Wu xing zhi mentions Hejian, and two characters are probably missing above.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Phases treatise adds “Hejian,” suggesting a lacuna.

sentences.zh: 」按：宋書五行志五亦有「河間」。

translations.literal: Comment: Song shu, Wu xing zhi 5 likewise has “Hejian.”
translations.idiomatic: Song shu confirms the Hejian wording.

sentences.zh: 東夷三國前後十餘輩 「十」，從宋本，他本作「千」。

translations.literal: Regarding “three eastern Yi states in more than ten parties”: “ten” follows the Song edition; other editions read “thousand.”
translations.idiomatic: Prefer Song’s “ten” over other editions’ absurd “thousand.”

sentences.zh: 丁亥郡國八雨雹 據本書五行志下，此爲五、六月間事，疑紀脫月。

translations.literal: Regarding dinghai and hail in eight commanderies: according to this book’s Wu xing zhi, part 2, the event belongs between the fifth and sixth months; the annals probably omit the month.
translations.idiomatic: Hail narrative likely dropped its month tag.

sentences.zh: 遣鎮軍將軍琅邪王伷出涂中 周校：「鎮軍將軍，當作鎮東大將軍，據泰始五年、太康三年及本傳文知之。

translations.literal: Regarding dispatching general who guards the army, king Zhou of Langye, out from Tu: Zhou’s collation says it should read great general who guards the east, based on Taishi 5, Taikang 3, and his biography.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhou’s title should be “guard the east,” not “guard the army.”

sentences.zh: 」按：周說當是，吳志孫皓傳亦作「鎮東大將軍司馬伷」，此時鎮軍爲司馬攸，與伷無涉。

translations.literal: Comment: Zhou’s view is correct; Wu zhi, Sun Hao’s biography, likewise has great general who guards the east Sima Zhou, while at this time “guard the army” was Sima You, unrelated to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjian and Wu zhi agree; “guard the army” belongs to Sima You.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍將軍留憲 斠注：「王濬傳『鎮軍』作『鎮南』。

translations.literal: Regarding general who guards the army Liu Xian: the collation note says Wang Jun’s biography writes “guard the south.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun’s memoir says “southern” general for Liu Xian.

sentences.zh: 」按：本書杜預傳、冊府元龜以下簡稱冊府三五〇「留憲」作「劉憲」。

translations.literal: Comment: Du Yu’s biography in this book and Cefu yuangui 350 write the name as Liu Xian with the surname Liu, whereas the annals write Liu Xian with the graph liu meaning “to stay.”
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu’s memoir and the Cefu quotation spell the commander’s name as Liu Xian; the annals use the homophone “stay” for the surname syllable.

sentences.zh: 斬吳江陵都督伍延 「伍延」，各本皆作「王延」。

translations.literal: Regarding beheading Wu’s Jiangling commander Wu Yan: editions all write Wang Yan instead of Wu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Editions misprint the surname as Wang.

sentences.zh: 按：本書杜預傳、吳志孫皓傳、冊府一二一、通鑑八一皆作「伍延」，今據改。

translations.literal: Comment: Du Yu’s biography, Wu zhi, Cefu yuangui 121, and Zizhi tongjian 81 all have Wu Yan; emend accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Major parallels read Wu Yan; adopt that form.

sentences.zh: 參周校及洪頤烜諸史考異。

translations.literal: See Zhou’s collation and Hong Yixuan’s Zhu shi kaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: See Zhou and Hong for discussion.

sentences.zh: 三月壬寅至石頭 「壬寅」，各本皆作「壬申」。

translations.literal: Regarding third month renyin reaching Shitou: editions all read renshen instead of renyin.
translations.idiomatic: Renshen is a graphic error for renyin.

sentences.zh: 按：三月戊子朔，無壬申。

translations.literal: Comment: third month begins wuzi new moon, so renshen cannot occur.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar excludes renshen.

sentences.zh: 校文云，王濬傳載濬入石頭後上書有「以十五日至秣陵」語，十五日爲壬寅，則「申」當爲「寅」字之誤。

translations.literal: Collation states that Wang Jun’s memorial after entering Shitou says “on the fifteenth day I reached Moling”; the fifteenth is renyin, so shen must be a mistake for yin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun’s date fixes the graph as yin.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: Therefore emend on this evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Editors change shen to yin.

sentences.zh: 乙酉 三月戊子朔，無乙酉。

translations.literal: Regarding yiyou: third month begins wuzi new moon, so yiyou does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyou is impossible in that third month.

sentences.zh: 通鑑八一作「四月乙酉」，爲四月二十九日。

translations.literal: Zizhi tongjian 81 places yiyou in the fourth month as the twenty-ninth day.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjian moves the amnesty to fourth month yiyou.

sentences.zh: 丙寅 五月丁亥朔，無丙寅。

translations.literal: Regarding bingyin: fifth month begins dinghai new moon, so bingyin does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Bingyin cannot fall in that fifth month.

sentences.zh: 丙寅及此下丁卯、庚午、庚辰、丁丑、甲申，皆在六月內，下文「丁丑」前「六月」二字應在「丙寅」上。

translations.literal: Bingyin together with dingmao, gengwu, gengchen, and dingchou below all fall within the sixth month; the two characters “sixth month” before dingchou below should stand before bingyin.
translations.idiomatic: The month label “sixth month” is misplaced; several stem dates belong to June.

sentences.zh: 又庚辰爲六月二十五日，丁丑爲二十二日，日序亦倒。

translations.literal: Moreover gengchen is the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month and dingchou the twenty-second, so the day order is inverted.
translations.idiomatic: Even within June the stems are out of sequence.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑慕容廆寇昌黎 「慕容廆」，通鑑八一作「涉歸」。

translations.literal: Regarding “Murong Hui of the Xianbei raided Changli”: Zizhi tongjian 81 writes Shegui instead of Murong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjian names Shegui as the raider.

sentences.zh: 通鑑考異：「按范亨燕書武宣紀。

translations.literal: Tongjian kaoyi: according to Fan Heng’s Yan shu, “Basic annals of Martial and Xuan.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang cites Fan Heng’s Former Yan record.

sentences.zh: 廆泰始五年生，年十五，父單于涉歸卒，太康四年也。

translations.literal: Murong Hui was born in Taishi 5 and was fifteen when his father, chanyu Shegui, died in Taikang 4.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui’s birth year makes him too young for this raid.

sentences.zh: 此年入寇，當是涉歸。」

translations.literal: The raid this year must therefore have been led by Shegui.”
translations.idiomatic: The attacker should be Shegui, not his teen son.”

sentences.zh: 秋七月 「七月」，從宋本。

translations.literal: Regarding autumn seventh month: “seventh month” follows the Song edition.
translations.idiomatic: The month reading follows Song.

sentences.zh: 明吳氏西爽堂本以下簡稱吳本同宋本，他本皆作「八月」。

translations.literal: Ming Wu’s Xishuangtang edition matches Song; other editions read “eighth month.”
translations.idiomatic: Later prints wrongly shift the month to August.

sentences.zh: 鎮東大將軍琅邪王伷爲撫軍將軍 周校：「『撫軍』衍文，據明年伷薨文及職官志、本傳知之。」

translations.literal: Regarding great general who guards the east, king Zhou of Langye, as “pacification general”: Zhou’s collation says the words “pacification general” are a gloss and should be deleted, judging from his death next year, the Offices treatise, and his biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou argues “pacification general” is a stray interpolation for Sima Zhou.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月甲申 正月辛丑朔，無甲申。

translations.literal: Regarding Taikang 4, spring, first month, jiashen: first month begins xinchou new moon, so jiashen does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Jiashen cannot open Taikang 4.

sentences.zh: 二月辛未朔，甲申爲是月十四日。

translations.literal: Second month begins xinwei new moon, so jiashen is the fourteenth day of the second month.
translations.idiomatic: Jiashen belongs in the second month instead.

sentences.zh: 三月辛丑朔 三月庚子朔，辛丑爲初二日。

translations.literal: Regarding “third month xinchou new moon”: third month begins gengzi new moon, so xinchou is the second day.
translations.idiomatic: If the month truly begins gengzi, xinchou is day two.

sentences.zh: 「朔」字疑衍，或「辛丑」爲「庚子」之誤。

translations.literal: The character “new moon” is probably redundant, or xinchou is a mistake for gengzi.
translations.idiomatic: Either drop “new moon” or fix xinchou to gengzi.

sentences.zh: 南宮王子玷爲長樂王 安平獻王孚傳「玷」作「祐」，太平寰宇記六三亦作「祐」。

translations.literal: Regarding “Prince Dian of the southern palace as king of Changle”: the biography of Prince Xian of Anping writes the name You, and Taiping huanyu ji 63 also writes You.
translations.idiomatic: Parallel texts read You, not Dian, for this prince.

sentences.zh: 正月甲申朔 正月庚申朔，甲申爲二十五日，疑「甲」爲「庚」字之誤。

translations.literal: Regarding first month jiashen new moon: first month begins gengshen new moon, so jiashen is the twenty-fifth day; jia is probably a mistake for geng.
translations.idiomatic: The first-day label may misprint gengshen as jiashen.

sentences.zh: 下文「戊辰」爲初九日，如作「甲申」，日序不合。

translations.literal: The wuchen below is the ninth day; if one reads jiashen, the sequence fails.
translations.idiomatic: Internal chronology requires gengshen, not jiashen.

sentences.zh: 齊國天水隕霜 「天水」，各本皆作「大水」。

translations.literal: Regarding Qi principality and Tianshui killing frost: editions all write “great flood” instead of “Tianshui.”
translations.idiomatic: A water/frost confusion mars this line.

sentences.zh: 周校：五行志，四月齊國、天水二郡隕霜，『大水』爲『天水』之誤。

translations.literal: Zhou’s collation: the Wu xing zhi says fourth month Qi and Tianshui commanderies had killing frost; “great flood” is a mistake for “Tianshui.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhou cites the treatise to restore Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 按：宋書五行志四亦作「天水」，今據改。

translations.literal: Comment: Song shu, Wu xing zhi 4 likewise has “Tianshui”; emend accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Song shu confirms Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 立河間平王洪子英爲章武王 本書河間王洪傳稱，洪二子威、混，無名英者。

translations.literal: Regarding establishing Ying, son of Hejian’s peaceful king Hong, as king of Zhangwu: the biography of Hejian king Hong lists only two sons, Wei and Hun, and none named Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Hong’s biography lacks a son Ying.

sentences.zh: 威嗣洪，徙封章武。

translations.literal: Wei succeeded Hong and was transferred to be king of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei inherited then moved to Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 其後威出繼義陽王望，又立混爲嗣。

translations.literal: Later Wei went out to succeed Prince Wang of Yiyang, and Hun was established as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Succession shifts to Hun after Wei’s transfer.

sentences.zh: 傳云威出繼在太康九年，與英受封章武王正在同年。

translations.literal: The biography says Wei’s transfer came in Taikang 9, the same year Ying received Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: The chronology overlaps Wei’s move with “Ying’s” enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 成紀咸和六年下有以「章武王混子珍爲章武王」之文，則此處「英」當爲「混」字之誤。

translations.literal: The Chengji annals under Xianhe 6 record later that “Zhangwu king Hun’s son Zhen was made Zhangwu king,” so here “Ying” should be the graph Hun miswritten.
translations.idiomatic: Later text shows Hun’s line; “Ying” should read Hun.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚寅 十二月辛卯朔，無庚寅。

translations.literal: Regarding twelfth month gengyin: twelfth month begins xinmao new moon, so gengyin does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyin is absent from that December.

sentences.zh: 五行志上、宋書五行志一、通典五一引河南孫平子封事並作十一月。

translations.literal: Wu xing zhi, part 1, Song shu Wu xing zhi 1, and Tongdian 51’s quotation of Henan Sun Pingzi’s memorial all place the event in the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Parallels set the temple-beam break in November.

sentences.zh: 庚寅爲十一月二十九日。

translations.literal: Gengyin is the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: That makes gengyin the eleventh month’s penultimate day.

sentences.zh: 虜奚軻男女十萬口來降 「奚軻」上各本皆有「壬戌」二字。

translations.literal: Regarding “one hundred thousand persons of the Xihe tribe came to surrender”: editions all insert the two characters renxu above Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Spurious renxu precedes the tribal name in some prints.

sentences.zh: 按：「是歲」下不應再出干支，「虜壬戌奚軻」，文義亦不可通。

translations.literal: Comment: after “that year” one should not again give a stem-branch; “captives renxu Xihe” is unintelligible.
translations.idiomatic: The stray stem breaks syntax after “that year.”

sentences.zh: 冊府九七七、通鑑八二皆無「壬戌」，今據刪。

translations.literal: Cefu yuangui 977 and Zizhi tongjian 82 lack renxu; delete per their witness.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjian and Cefu omit renxu; editors delete it.
